sentences.zh: 楊慎，字用修，新都人，少師廷和子也。

translations.literal: Yang Shen, styled Yongxiu, was a native of Xindu and the son of Junior Tutor Yang Tinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen, styled Yongxiu, was from Xindu and the son of the Junior Tutor Yang Tinghe.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，舉正德六年殿試第一，授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: At the age of twenty-four he took first place in the palace examination of the sixth year of Zhengde and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four he ranked first in the palace examination of Zhengde 6 (1511) and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，服闋起故官。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his stepmother; when the mourning period ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his stepmother, he returned to his former office when the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，武宗微行，始出居庸關，慎抗疏切諫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year, when Emperor Wuzong traveled incognito and first passed beyond Juyong Pass, Shen submitted a forthright memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year (1517), when the emperor traveled incognito and first went beyond Juyong Pass, Shen submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 尋移疾歸。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，起充經筵講官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Shen was recalled to serve as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Shen was recalled to serve as a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 常講《舜典》，言：「聖人設贖刑，乃施於小過，俾民自新。

translations.literal: He often lectured on the Canon of Shun and said: "When the sage instituted ransom punishments, it was to apply to minor offenses, so that the people might reform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In lecturing on the Canon of Shun he said, "The sage instituted ransom punishments for minor offenses so that the people might reform themselves.

sentences.zh: 若元惡大奸，無可贖之理。」

translations.literal: As for arch-villains and great traitors, there is no principle by which they may be ransomed.
translations.idiomatic: For arch-villains and great traitors, there is no principle of ransom.

sentences.zh: 時大榼張銳、於經論死，或言進金銀獲宥，故及之。

translations.literal: At the time the grand eunuchs Zhang Rui and Yu Jing had been sentenced to death, and some said they had been pardoned for offering gold and silver—hence he touched on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the grand eunuchs Zhang Rui and Yu Jing had been sentenced to death amid talk that they had been spared for offering gold and silver—hence his remark.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，帝納桂萼、張璁言，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing the emperor accepted the proposals of Gui E and Zhang Cong and summoned them as Hanlin Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 (1524) the emperor accepted the proposals of Gui E and Zhang Cong and summoned them as Hanlin Academicians.

sentences.zh: 慎偕同列三十六人上言：「臣等與萼輩學術不同，議論亦異。

translations.literal: Shen together with thirty-six colleagues of his rank submitted a memorial saying: "We and Gui E's party differ in learning and in opinion as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and thirty-six colleagues submitted a memorial: "We and Gui E's party differ in scholarship and in opinion.

sentences.zh: 臣等所執者，程頤、朱熹之說也。

translations.literal: What we uphold is the teaching of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: What we uphold is the teaching of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 萼等所執者，冷褒、段猶之余也。

translations.literal: What Gui E and his party uphold is the remnant of Leng Bao and Duan You.
translations.idiomatic: What Gui E's party upholds is the remnant doctrine of Leng Bao and Duan You.

sentences.zh: 今陛下既超擢萼輩，不以臣等言為是，臣等不能與同列，願賜罷斥。」

translations.literal: Now that Your Majesty has promoted Gui E's party above their due rank and does not regard our words as correct, we cannot remain in the same ranks with them and beg to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has promoted Gui E's party and does not accept our view, we cannot remain in the same ranks with them and beg to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責，停俸有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, sharply rebuked them, and suspended their salaries in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, sharply rebuked them, and suspended their salaries to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 逾月，又偕學士豐熙等疏諫。

translations.literal: After more than a month he again joined Academician Feng Xi and others in a memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later he again joined Academician Feng Xi and others in a memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 不得命，偕廷臣伏左順門力諫。

translations.literal: Receiving no response, he joined the court officials in prostrating themselves at the Left Gate of Compliance to remonstrate with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving no answer, he joined court officials in prostrating themselves at the Left Gate of Compliance to remonstrate forcefully.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，命執首事八人下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered the eight leaders seized and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered the eight ringleaders seized and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 於是慎及檢討王元正等撼門大哭，聲徹殿庭。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shen and Compiler Wang Yuanzheng and others beat on the gate and wept aloud, their voices filling the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shen, Compiler Wang Yuanzheng, and others beat on the gate and wept aloud until their voices filled the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，悉下詔獄，廷杖之。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier, had them all sent to the imperial prison, and had them beaten with rods at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier, had them all imprisoned, and had them flogged at court.

sentences.zh: 閱十日，有言前此朝罷，群臣已散，慎、元正及給事中劉濟、安磐、張漢卿、張原，御史王時柯實糾眾伏哭。

translations.literal: Ten days later it was reported that on the previous occasion, after court had adjourned and the officials had dispersed, it was Shen, Yuanzheng, Supervising Secretary Liu Ji, An Pan, Zhang Hanqing, Zhang Yuan, and Censor Wang Shike who had actually rallied the crowd to prostrate themselves and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later it was reported that after court had adjourned and the officials had dispersed, it was Shen, Yuanzheng, Supervising Secretary Liu Ji, An Pan, Zhang Hanqing, Zhang Yuan, and Censor Wang Shike who had actually rallied the crowd to prostrate themselves and weep.

sentences.zh: 乃再杖七人於廷。

translations.literal: The seven were therefore beaten with rods at court again.
translations.idiomatic: The seven were therefore flogged at court again.

sentences.zh: 慎、元正、濟並謫戍，余削籍。

translations.literal: Shen, Yuanzheng, and Ji were all banished to frontier garrison service; the rest were struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, Yuanzheng, and Ji were all banished to frontier garrison service; the others were struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 慎得雲南永昌衛。

translations.literal: Shen was assigned to Yongchang Guard in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was assigned to Yongchang Guard in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 先是，廷和當國，盡斥錦衣冒濫官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tinghe held power, he had dismissed all the improperly appointed officials in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Tinghe held power, he had dismissed all improperly appointed officials in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 及是伺諸途，將害慎。

translations.literal: Now they lay in wait along the route, intending to harm Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Now they lay in wait along the route, intending to harm Shen.

sentences.zh: 慎知而謹備之。

translations.literal: Shen learned of it and took careful precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Shen learned of it and took careful precautions.

sentences.zh: 至臨清始散去。

translations.literal: Only when he reached Linqing did they finally disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he reached Linqing did they finally disperse.

sentences.zh: 扶病馳萬里，憊甚。

translations.literal: Supporting himself in illness he raced ten thousand li and was utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Supporting himself through illness, he raced ten thousand li and was utterly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 抵戍所，幾不起。

translations.literal: When he reached his place of banishment he nearly could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached his place of banishment he nearly could not get up.

sentences.zh: 五年聞廷和疾，馳至家。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, hearing that Tinghe was ill, he raced home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, hearing that Tinghe was ill, he raced home.

sentences.zh: 廷和喜，疾愈。

translations.literal: Tinghe was delighted and recovered from his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe was delighted and recovered from his illness.

sentences.zh: 還永昌，聞尋甸安銓、武定鳳朝文作亂，率僮奴及步卒百余，馳赴木密所與守臣擊敗賊。

translations.literal: Returning to Yongchang, he heard that An Qian of Xundian and Feng Chaowen of Wuding had risen in rebellion; he led more than a hundred Zhuang retainers and foot soldiers in a forced march to Mumi post, where together with the defending officials he defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Yongchang, he heard that An Qian of Xundian and Feng Chaowen of Wuding had rebelled; he led more than a hundred Zhuang retainers and foot soldiers in a forced march to Mumi post, where with the defending officials he defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 八年聞廷和訃，奔告巡撫歐陽重請於朝，獲歸葬，葬訖復還。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, hearing of Tinghe's death, he rushed to inform Grand Coordinator Ouyang Chong and petitioned the court; he was permitted to return and bury him, and after the burial he went back again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, hearing of Tinghe's death, he rushed to inform Grand Coordinator Ouyang Chong and petitioned the court; permitted to return for the burial, he went back to banishment after the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 自是，或歸蜀，或居雲南會城，或留戍所，大吏鹹善視之。

translations.literal: From then on he would sometimes return to Shu, sometimes live in the Yunnan provincial capital, sometimes remain at his garrison post; the high officials all treated him kindly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he sometimes returned to Shu, sometimes lived in the Yunnan provincial capital, sometimes remained at his garrison post; the senior officials all treated him kindly.

sentences.zh: 及年七十，還蜀，巡撫遣四指揮逮之還。

translations.literal: When he reached seventy he returned to Shu; the grand coordinator sent four commanders to seize him and bring him back.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached seventy he returned to Shu; the grand coordinator sent four commanders to seize him and bring him back.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年七月卒，年七十有二。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of Jiajing 38 (1559), aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 慎幼警敏，十一歲能詩。

translations.literal: From childhood Shen was keen and quick; at eleven he could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Shen was keen and quick; at eleven he could compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 十二擬作《古戰場文》、《過秦論》，長老驚異。

translations.literal: At twelve he drafted essays in the manner of "An Ancient Battlefield" and "On the Fall of Qin," and the elders were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he drafted essays in the manner of "An Ancient Battlefield" and "On the Fall of Qin," to the astonishment of his elders.

sentences.zh: 入京，賦《黃葉詩》，李東陽見而嗟賞，令受業門下。

translations.literal: On entering the capital he composed "Poem on Yellow Leaves"; Li Dongyang saw it, sighed in admiration, and had him study under his tutelage.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the capital he composed "Poem on Yellow Leaves"; Li Dongyang saw it, sighed in admiration, and took him as a pupil.

sentences.zh: 在翰林時，武宗問欽天監及翰林：「星有註張，又作汪張，是何星也？」

translations.literal: While in the Hanlin Academy, Emperor Wuzong asked the Directorate of Astronomy and the Hanlin: "There is a star written Zhu Zhang, also written Wang Zhang—what star is this?
translations.idiomatic: While in the Hanlin Academy, Emperor Wuzong asked the Directorate of Astronomy and the Hanlin, "There is a star written Zhu Zhang, also written Wang Zhang—what star is this?

sentences.zh: 眾不能對。

translations.literal: No one could answer.
translations.idiomatic: No one could answer.

sentences.zh: 慎曰：「柳星也。」

translations.literal: Shen said: "It is the Willow Star.
translations.idiomatic: Shen said, "It is the Willow Star.

sentences.zh: 歷舉《周禮》、《史記》、《漢書》以復。

translations.literal: He cited in turn the Rites of Zhou, the Records of the Grand Historian, and the Book of Han in reply.
translations.idiomatic: He cited in turn the Rites of Zhou, the Records of the Grand Historian, and the Book of Han in reply.

sentences.zh: 預修《武宗實錄》，事必直書。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong and recorded events with strict fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong and recorded events with strict fidelity.

sentences.zh: 總裁蔣冕、費宏盡付稿草，俾削定。

translations.literal: The chief compilers Jiang Mian and Fei Hong turned over all draft manuscripts to him for revision and final editing.
translations.idiomatic: Chief compilers Jiang Mian and Fei Hong turned over all draft manuscripts to him for revision and final editing.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉使過鎮江，謁楊一清，閱所藏書。

translations.literal: Once on a mission he passed through Zhenjiang and called on Yang Yiqing, examining his collected books.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a mission he passed through Zhenjiang and called on Yang Yiqing, examining his library.

sentences.zh: 叩以疑義，一清皆成誦。

translations.literal: He raised doubtful points, and Yiqing recited the answers from memory in every case.
translations.idiomatic: He raised doubtful points, and Yiqing recited the answers from memory in every case.

sentences.zh: 慎驚異，益肆力古學。

translations.literal: Shen was astonished and applied himself all the more vigorously to classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was astonished and applied himself all the more vigorously to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 既投荒多暇，書無所不覽。

translations.literal: Once cast into exile with much leisure, he read books of every kind.
translations.idiomatic: Once cast into exile with much leisure, he read books of every kind.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「資性不足恃。

translations.literal: He once told others: "Native endowment is not something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: He once told others, "Native talent is not something to rely on.

sentences.zh: 日新德業，當自學問中來。」

translations.literal: Daily renewal of virtue and achievement must come from learning.
translations.idiomatic: Daily renewal of virtue and achievement must come from learning.

sentences.zh: 故好學窮理，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Therefore he loved learning and pursued principle to the utmost, growing only more devoted in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he loved learning and pursued principle to the utmost, growing only more devoted in old age.

sentences.zh: 世宗以議禮故，惡其父子特甚。

translations.literal: Because of the Rites Controversy, Emperor Shizong hated father and son with special bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the Rites Controversy, Emperor Shizong hated father and son with special bitterness.

sentences.zh: 每問慎作何狀，閣臣以老病對，乃稍解。

translations.literal: Whenever he asked what Shen was doing, the grand secretaries answered that he was old and ill, and the emperor's anger eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he asked what Shen was doing, the grand secretaries answered that he was old and ill, and the emperor's anger eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 慎聞之，益縱酒自放。

translations.literal: When Shen heard of this he indulged in wine all the more and let himself go.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen heard of this he indulged in wine all the more and let himself go.

sentences.zh: 明世記誦之博，著作之富，推慎為第一。

translations.literal: In the Ming age, for breadth of memorization and wealth of writings, Shen was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming age, for breadth of memorization and wealth of writings, Shen was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 詩文外，雜著至一百余種，並行於世。

translations.literal: Apart from poetry and prose, his miscellaneous works numbered more than a hundred kinds, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from poetry and prose, his miscellaneous works numbered more than a hundred kinds, all circulating in his day.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，追謚文憲。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the temple name Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 王元正，字舜卿，盩厔人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanzheng, styled Shunqing, was a native of Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanzheng, styled Shunqing, was from Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 與慎同年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the same year as Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the same year as Shen.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授檢討。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 武宗幸宣、大，元正述《五子之歌》以諷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong visited Xuanfu and Datong, Yuanzheng expounded the "Song of the Five Sons" as indirect admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong visited Xuanfu and Datong, Yuanzheng expounded the "Song of the Five Sons" as indirect admonition.

sentences.zh: 竟以爭「大禮」，謫戍茂州卒。

translations.literal: In the end, for disputing the "Great Rites," he was banished to garrison service at Maozhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, for disputing the Great Rites, he was banished to garrison service at Maozhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously granted the title of Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously granted the title of Compiler.

sentences.zh: 王思，字宜學，太保直曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Si, styled Yixue, was the great-grandson of Grand Mentor Wang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si, styled Yixue, was the great-grandson of Grand Mentor Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Zhengde 6 (1511).

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Editor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Editor.

sentences.zh: 九年春，乾清宮災。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year the Palace of Heavenly Purity caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year (1514) the Palace of Heavenly Purity caught fire.

sentences.zh: 思應詔上疏曰：「天下之治賴紀綱，紀綱之立系君身而已。

translations.literal: Si responded to the edict with a memorial saying: "The governance of the realm depends on discipline and standards; the establishment of discipline and standards rests on the person of the ruler alone.
translations.idiomatic: Si responded to the edict with a memorial: "The governance of the realm depends on discipline and standards, and discipline and standards rest on the ruler alone.

sentences.zh: 私恩不偏於近習，政柄不移於左右，則紀綱立，而宰輔得行其誌，六卿得專其職。

translations.literal: If private favor is not biased toward those close at hand and the handles of government are not shifted to attendants at one's side, then discipline and standards are established, the chief ministers can carry out their aims, and the six ministers can devote themselves to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: If private favor is not biased toward intimates and the handles of government are not shifted to attendants, discipline and standards are established, the chief ministers can carry out their aims, and the six ministers can devote themselves to their duties.

sentences.zh: 今者內閣執奏方堅，而或撓於傳奉，六卿擬議已定，而或阻於內批，此紀綱所由廢也。

translations.literal: Now the inner cabinet's memorials are firm when submitted, yet sometimes they are thwarted by transmitted orders; the six ministers' deliberations are settled, yet sometimes they are blocked by inner rescripts—this is how discipline and standards come to be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Today the inner cabinet's memorials are firm when submitted, yet sometimes they are thwarted by transmitted orders; the six ministers' deliberations are settled, yet sometimes they are blocked by inner rescripts—this is how discipline and standards are abandoned.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下抑私恩，端政本，用舍不以讒移，刑賞不以私拒，則體統正而朝廷尊矣。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty restrains private favor, rectifies the root of government, does not shift appointments and dismissals because of slander, and does not withhold punishments and rewards for private reasons will the institutional order be correct and the court honored.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty restrains private favor, rectifies the root of government, does not shift appointments because of slander, and does not withhold punishments and rewards for private reasons will the institutional order be correct and the court honored.

sentences.zh: 祖宗故事，正朝之外，日奏事左順門，又不時召對便殿。

translations.literal: By the precedents of the ancestral house, apart from the regular court audience, affairs were reported daily at the Left Gate of Compliance, and the ruler also summoned ministers for consultation in the side hall from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: By ancestral precedent, apart from the regular court audience, affairs were reported daily at the Left Gate of Compliance, and the ruler also summoned ministers for consultation in the side hall from time to time.

sentences.zh: 今每月御朝不過三五日，每朝進奏不逾一二事。

translations.literal: Now the ruler holds court no more than three or five days a month, and at each audience no more than one or two matters are reported.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ruler holds court no more than three or five days a month, and at each audience no more than one or two matters are reported.

sentences.zh: 其養德之功，求治之實，宰輔不得而知也。

translations.literal: As for the achievements of cultivating virtue and the realities of seeking good governance, the chief ministers cannot know them.
translations.idiomatic: The achievements of cultivating virtue and the realities of seeking good governance are things the chief ministers cannot know.

sentences.zh: 聞見之非，嗜好之過，宰輔不得而知也。

translations.literal: Errors in what is heard and seen, excesses in likes and preferences—the chief ministers cannot know them.
translations.idiomatic: Errors in what the ruler hears and sees, excesses in his likes and preferences—the chief ministers cannot know them.

sentences.zh: 天下之大，四海之遠，生民愁苦之狀，盜賊縱橫之由，豈能一一上達？

translations.literal: Given the vastness of the realm and the remoteness of the four seas, how can the people's distress and the causes of banditry all reach the throne one by one?
translations.idiomatic: In a realm so vast and seas so distant, how can every report of the people's misery and every cause of banditry reach the throne?

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下悉遵舊典，凡遇宴間，少賜召問。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will fully follow the old precedents and, whenever feasts occur, graciously summon and inquire a little.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to follow the old precedents fully and, at feasts, summon ministers for consultation more often.

sentences.zh: 勿以遇災而懼，災過而弛，然後可以享天心，保天命。」

translations.literal: Do not fear only when disasters strike and relax once they pass; only then can you enjoy Heaven's favor and preserve Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Do not dread calamities only when they occur and grow lax once they pass; only then can you enjoy Heaven's favor and preserve Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，帝狎虎而傷，閱月不視朝。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month, the emperor was injured while playing with a tiger and for a full month did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the ninth month, the emperor was injured while playing with a tiger and did not hold court for a full month.

sentences.zh: 思復上封事曰：「孝宗皇帝之子惟陛下一人，當為天下萬世自重。

translations.literal: Si again submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Emperor Xiaozong had only Your Majesty as his son; you ought to prize yourself for the sake of the realm and all generations to come.
translations.idiomatic: Si again submitted a sealed memorial: "Emperor Xiaozong had only Your Majesty as his son; you must value yourself for the sake of the realm and all generations to come.

sentences.zh: 近者道路傳言，虎逸於柙，驚及聖躬。

translations.literal: Recently rumors on the roads say a tiger escaped its cage and alarmed Your Majesty's sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: Recently rumors on the roads say a tiger escaped its cage and alarmed Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之，且駭且懼。

translations.literal: When I heard this, I was both shocked and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard this, I was shocked and afraid.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，於茲九年。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty acceded to the throne, nine years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years have passed since Your Majesty acceded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朝寧不勤政，太廟不親享。

translations.literal: Court audiences are rarely held with diligence; the Imperial Ancestral Temple is not personally attended for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences are rarely held with diligence, and the Imperial Ancestral Temple is not personally attended for offerings.

sentences.zh: 兩宮曠於問安，經筵倦於聽講。

translations.literal: Visits to inquire after the two palaces are neglected; the classics lecture is attended with weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Visits to inquire after the two palaces are neglected, and the classics lecture is attended with weariness.

sentences.zh: 揆厥所自，蓋有二端：嗜酒而荒其誌，好勇而輕其身。

translations.literal: Tracing this to its source, there are roughly two causes: love of wine that wastes one's purpose, and love of valor that makes light of one's person.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing this to its source, there are two causes: a love of wine that wastes one's purpose, and a love of valor that makes light of one's person.

sentences.zh: 由是，戒懼之心日忘，縱恣之欲日進，好惡由乎喜怒，政令出於多門。

translations.literal: From this, the heart of caution and fear is daily forgotten, the desires of indulgence daily advance, likes and dislikes follow joy and anger, and government orders issue from many gates.
translations.idiomatic: From this, caution and fear are daily forgotten, indulgence daily grows, likes and dislikes follow whims of joy and anger, and government orders issue from many quarters.

sentences.zh: 紀綱積弛。

translations.literal: Discipline and standards have been steadily loosened.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline and standards have steadily loosened.

sentences.zh: 國是不立。

translations.literal: The fundamental policies of the state are not established.
translations.idiomatic: The fundamental policies of the state are not established.

sentences.zh: 士氣摧折，人心危疑。

translations.literal: The spirit of the scholar-officials is broken down; men's hearts are anxious and uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of the scholar-officials is broken, and men's hearts are anxious and uncertain.

sentences.zh: 上天示警，日食地震。

translations.literal: Heaven shows warnings: eclipses of the sun and earthquakes.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven shows warnings in solar eclipses and earthquakes.

sentences.zh: 宗社之憂，凜若朝夕。

translations.literal: Anxiety for the altars of state and ancestral temple is as pressing as morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Anxiety for the altars of state and ancestral temple presses as if morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 夫勇不可好，陛下已薄有所懲矣。

translations.literal: Valor ought not to be loved; Your Majesty has already been somewhat punished for it.
translations.idiomatic: Valor ought not to be indulged; Your Majesty has already been somewhat chastened for it.

sentences.zh: 至於荒誌廢業，惟酒為甚。

translations.literal: As for wasting purpose and abandoning work, wine is the worst.
translations.idiomatic: As for wasting purpose and abandoning duty, nothing is worse than wine.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『甘酒嗜音，峻宇雕墻，有一於此，未或不亡。』

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Sweet wine, love of music, lofty halls and carved walls—if there is any one of these, none fail eventually to perish."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Sweet wine, love of music, lofty halls and carved walls—if there is any one of these, none fail eventually to perish.

sentences.zh: 陛下露處外宮，日湎於酒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells in the open at an outer palace, daily drowned in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dwells in the open at an outer palace, drowned in wine every day.

sentences.zh: 廝養雜侍，禁衛不嚴。

translations.literal: Menials and attendants wait on you in a mixed crowd; the palace guard is not strict.
translations.idiomatic: Menials and attendants wait on you in a mixed crowd, and the palace guard is not strict.

sentences.zh: 即不幸變起倉卒，何以備之？

translations.literal: If misfortune should rise suddenly, how would you be prepared?
translations.idiomatic: If misfortune should arise suddenly, how would you be prepared?

sentences.zh: 此臣所大憂也。」

translations.literal: This is what your servant greatly fears.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I greatly fear.

sentences.zh: 疏入，留中者數日，忽傳旨降遠方雜職，遂謫潮州三河驛丞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was kept at court for several days; suddenly an order was transmitted to demote him to a miscellaneous post in a distant place, and he was banished to be assistant magistrate of the Sanhe Postal Station in Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, it was kept at court for several days; then an order suddenly came to demote him to a miscellaneous post in a distant place, and he was banished to assistant magistrate of the Sanhe Postal Station in Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 思年少氣銳，每眾中指切人是非。

translations.literal: In his youth Si was sharp-spirited and often pointed out others' right and wrong before assembled company.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Si was sharp-spirited and often pointed out others' faults before assembled company.

sentences.zh: 已悔之，自斂為質訥。

translations.literal: Having come to regret this, he restrained himself and became plain and taciturn.
translations.idiomatic: Having come to regret this, he restrained himself and became plain and taciturn.

sentences.zh: 及被謫，怡然就道。

translations.literal: When he was banished, he went on his way with serene contentment.
translations.idiomatic: When he was banished, he went on his way with serene contentment.

sentences.zh: 夜過瀧水，舟飄巨石上，緣石坐浩歌。

translations.literal: One night crossing the Long Rapids, his boat drifted onto a great rock; he sat on the rock and sang loudly.
translations.idiomatic: One night crossing the Long Rapids, his boat drifted onto a great rock; he sat on the rock and sang loudly.

sentences.zh: 家人後至，聞歌聲乃艤舟以濟。

translations.literal: His family arrived later; hearing his singing, they moored the boat and crossed to join him.
translations.idiomatic: His family arrived later; hearing his singing, they moored the boat and crossed to join him.

sentences.zh: 王守仁講學贛州，思從之遊。

translations.literal: When Wang Shouren lectured in Ganzhou, Si went to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shouren lectured in Ganzhou, Si went to study with him.

sentences.zh: 及守仁討宸濠，檄思贊軍議。

translations.literal: When Shouren campaigned against Chen Hao, the Prince of Ning, he summoned Si to assist in military counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren campaigned against the Prince of Ning, he summoned Si to assist in military counsel.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，召復故官，仍加俸一級。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Si was recalled to his former office and given an additional grade of salary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Si was recalled to his former office and given an additional grade of salary.

sentences.zh: 思疏辭，且言：「陛下欲作敢言之氣，以防壅蔽之奸，莫若省覽奏章，召見大臣，勿使邪僻阿徇之說蠱惑聖聽，則堯、舜之治可成。

translations.literal: Si submitted a memorial declining the appointment and said: "If Your Majesty wishes to foster a spirit of forthright speech to guard against the wicked who block and obscure, there is nothing better than reviewing memorials and summoning chief ministers; do not let crooked and fawning doctrines bewitch the sacred ear—then the governance of Yao and Shun can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Si submitted a memorial declining the appointment: "If Your Majesty wishes to foster forthright speech to guard against those who block and obscure the truth, review memorials and summon chief ministers; do not let crooked, fawning doctrines bewitch the imperial ear—then the governance of Yao and Shun can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 不然，縱加恩於先朝譴責之臣，抑末矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, even if favor is extended to ministers censured in the previous reign, it will be a trivial matter.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, even extending favor to ministers censured in the previous reign will be a trivial matter.

sentences.zh: 帝不允，因命近日遷俸者，皆不得辭。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it and therefore ordered that all who had recently received salary increases might not decline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not permit it and ordered that all who had recently received salary increases might not decline.

sentences.zh: 尋充經筵講官。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed lecturer for the classics lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed lecturer for the classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年與同官屢爭「大禮」，不報。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he repeatedly joined his colleagues in disputing the "Great Rites," but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 (1524) he repeatedly joined his colleagues in disputing the Great Rites, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 時張璁、桂萼、方獻夫為學士，思羞與同列，疏乞罷歸。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu were academicians; Si was ashamed to serve alongside them and submitted a memorial begging to be dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu were academicians; Si was ashamed to serve alongside them and submitted a memorial begging to be dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was not granted.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，偕廷臣伏左順門哭諫。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month he joined the court ministers in kneeling and weeping at the Left Gate of Compliance to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the seventh month, he joined the court ministers in kneeling and weeping at the Left Gate of Compliance to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，系之詔獄，杖三十。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, had them imprisoned in the imperial prison, and beat them thirty blows with the stick.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered, had them imprisoned in the imperial prison, and beat them thirty blows with the stick.

sentences.zh: 逾旬，再杖之。

translations.literal: After more than ten days they were beaten again.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days they were beaten again.

sentences.zh: 思與同官王相，給事中張原、毛玉、裴紹宗，御史張曰韜、胡瓊，郎中楊淮、胡璉，員外郎申良、張澯，主事安璽、仵瑜、臧應奎、余禎、殷承敘，司務李可登，凡十有七人，皆病創先後卒。

translations.literal: Si, together with his colleague Wang Xiang, Supervising Secretaries Zhang Yuan, Mao Yu, and Pei Shaozong, Censor Zhang Yuetao and Hu Qiong, Directors Yang Huai and Hu Lian, Section Members Shen Liang and Zhang Can, Chief Clerks An Xi, Wu Yu, Zang Yingkui, Yu Zhen, and Yin Chengxu, and Registrar Li Kedeng—in all seventeen persons—died one after another from their wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Si, together with his colleague Wang Xiang, Supervising Secretaries Zhang Yuan, Mao Yu, and Pei Shaozong, Censor Zhang Yuetao and Hu Qiong, Directors Yang Huai and Hu Lian, Section Members Shen Liang and Zhang Can, Chief Clerks An Xi, Wu Yu, Zang Yingkui, Yu Zhen, and Yin Chengxu, and Registrar Li Kedeng—in all seventeen persons—died one after another from their wounds.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，各蔭一子，贈官有差。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing each was granted a posthumous privilege for one son, and conferred offices of differing ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing each was granted a posthumous privilege for one son, and conferred offices of differing ranks.

sentences.zh: 思贈右諭德。

translations.literal: Si was posthumously granted the title of Right Sub-Reader.
translations.idiomatic: Si was posthumously granted the title of Right Sub-Reader.

sentences.zh: 思誌行邁流俗，與李中、鄒守益善。

translations.literal: Si's purpose and conduct surpassed conventional society; he was on good terms with Li Zhong and Zou Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: Si's purpose and conduct surpassed conventional society; he was on good terms with Li Zhong and Zou Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 高陵呂柟亟稱之，嘗曰：「聞過而喜似季路，欲寡未能似伯玉，則改齋其人也。」

translations.literal: Lü Shan of Gaoling praised him repeatedly and once said: "Delighted to hear of one's faults—like Zilu; wishing to have few desires but not yet succeeding—like Boyu—that is the man called Gai Zhai.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shan of Gaoling praised him repeatedly and once said: "Delighted to hear of one's faults—like Zilu; wishing to have few desires but not yet succeeding—like Boyu—that is the man called Gai Zhai.

sentences.zh: 改齋者，思別號也。

translations.literal: Gai Zhai was Si's style name.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Zhai was Si's style name.

sentences.zh: 王相，字懋卿，鄞人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiang, styled Maoqing, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang, styled Maoqing, was a native of Yin.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixteenth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Zhengde 16 (1521).

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授編修。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Editor.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Editor.

sentences.zh: 豪邁尚誌節。

translations.literal: He was bold and free-spirited and valued moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and free-spirited and valued moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 事親篤孝。

translations.literal: In serving his parents he was deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his parents he was deeply filial.

sentences.zh: 家貧屢空，晏如。

translations.literal: Though his household was poor and often destitute, he was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Though his household was poor and often destitute, he was at ease.

sentences.zh: 仕僅四年而卒。

translations.literal: He served in office only four years before he died.
translations.idiomatic: He served in office only four years before he died.

sentences.zh: 張翀，字習之，潼川人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, styled Xizhi, was a native of Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, styled Xizhi, was a native of Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Zhengde 6 (1511).

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，改刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was selected as Hanlin Bachelor and transferred to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as Hanlin Bachelor and transferred to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸，起戶科。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and returned home; later he was recalled to the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and returned home; later he was recalled to the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，詔罷天下額外貢獻。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne, an edict abolished extra tribute from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne, an edict abolished extra tribute from throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其明年，中都鎮守內官張陽復貢新茶。

translations.literal: The next year Zhang Yang, the inner official guarding Zhongdu, again presented tribute of new tea.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhang Yang, the eunuch guarding Zhongdu, again presented tribute of new tea.

sentences.zh: 禮部請遵詔禁，不許。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites requested that the edict be obeyed and the tribute forbidden; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites requested that the edict be obeyed and the tribute forbidden; permission was not granted.

sentences.zh: 翀言：「陛下詔墨未乾，旋即反汗，人將窺測朝廷，玩侮政令。

translations.literal: Chong said: "Your Majesty's edict ink is not yet dry, yet you immediately go back on your word; people will probe and test the court and treat government orders with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said: "Your Majesty's edict is not yet dry, yet you immediately go back on your word; people will probe the court and treat government orders with contempt.

sentences.zh: 且陽名貢茶，實雜致他物。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Yang's tribute is nominally tea, in fact other goods are mixed in.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though Yang's tribute is nominally tea, in fact other goods are mixed in.

sentences.zh: 四方效尤，何所抵極。

translations.literal: If the four quarters imitate this example, where will it end?
translations.idiomatic: If the four quarters imitate this example, where will it end?

sentences.zh: 願守前詔，無墮奸謀。」

translations.literal: I hope you will uphold the earlier edict and not fall into wicked schemes.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will uphold the earlier edict and not fall into wicked schemes.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 寧夏歲貢紅花，大為軍民害；

translations.literal: Ningxia's annual tribute of safflower greatly harmed soldiers and civilians;
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia's annual tribute of safflower greatly harmed soldiers and civilians;

sentences.zh: 內外鎮守官蒞任，率貢馬謝恩。

translations.literal: when military commissioners within and without took up their posts, they invariably presented horses in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: when military commissioners within and without took up their posts, they invariably presented horses in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 翀皆請罷之。

translations.literal: Chong requested that all these be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Chong requested that all these be abolished.

sentences.zh: 帝雖是其言，不能從。

translations.literal: Though the emperor agreed with his words, he could not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor agreed with his words, he could not follow them.

sentences.zh: 尋言：「中官出鎮，非太祖、太宗舊制。

translations.literal: Before long he said: "Eunuchs sent out to guard regions is not the old system of Taizu and Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he said: "Eunuchs sent out to guard regions is not the old system of Taizu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 景帝遭國家多故，偶一行之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi faced many troubles in the state, it was done once as an exception.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingdi faced many troubles in the state, it was done once as an exception.

sentences.zh: 謂內臣是朝廷家人，但有急事，令其來奏。

translations.literal: It was said that inner officials were household servants of the court and that, when urgent matters arose, they could be summoned to report.
translations.idiomatic: It was said that eunuchs were household servants of the court and that, when urgent matters arose, they could be summoned to report.

sentences.zh: 乃往歲宸濠謀叛，鎮守太監王宏反助為逆，內臣果足恃耶？

translations.literal: Yet in years past when Chen Hao, the Prince of Ning, plotted rebellion, the guarding eunuch Wang Hong instead helped the rebel—are inner officials truly to be relied upon?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Prince of Ning plotted rebellion in years past, the guarding eunuch Wang Hong instead helped the rebel—are eunuchs truly to be relied upon?

sentences.zh: 時平則坐享尊榮，肆毒百姓，遇變則心懷顧望，不恤封疆。

translations.literal: In peaceful times they sit enjoying honor and glory and poison the common people; when crises come they harbor second thoughts and do not care for the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In peaceful times they sit enjoying honor and glory and poison the common people; when crises come they harbor second thoughts and do not care for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 不可不亟罷。」

translations.literal: They must be abolished at once.
translations.idiomatic: They must be abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 後張孚敬為相，竟罷諸鎮守，其論實自翀發之。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhang Fu became chief minister, all the guarding posts were finally abolished; the argument in fact originated with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Fu became chief minister, all the guarding posts were finally abolished; the argument in fact originated with Chong.

sentences.zh: 屢遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 又言：「頃聞紫禁之內，禱祠繁興。

translations.literal: He also said: "I have recently heard that within the Forbidden City prayers and sacrifices have flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I have recently heard that within the Forbidden City prayers and sacrifices have flourished.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮內官十數輩，究習經典，講誦科儀，賞賚逾涯，寵幸日密。

translations.literal: More than a dozen inner officials of the Palace of Heavenly Purity thoroughly study the classics, recite ritual formulas, receive rewards beyond measure, and grow daily in imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen eunuchs of the Palace of Heavenly Purity thoroughly study the classics, recite ritual formulas, receive rewards beyond measure, and grow daily in imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 此由先朝罪人遺黨若太監崔文輩，挾邪術為嘗試計。

translations.literal: This is because remnant factions of criminals from the previous reign, such as the eunuch Cui Wen and his ilk, wield heterodox arts as a means of trial and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: This is because remnant factions of criminals from the previous reign, such as the eunuch Cui Wen and his ilk, wield heterodox arts as a means of trial and advancement.

sentences.zh: 陛下為其愚弄，而已得肆其奸欺。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is befooled by them, and they are already free to practice their wicked deceits.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is befooled by them, and they are already free to practice their wicked deceits.

sentences.zh: 幹撓政事，牽引群邪，傷太平之業，失四海之望。

translations.literal: They interfere in government affairs, draw in a host of evildoers, injure the enterprise of great peace, and lose the hopes of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: They interfere in government affairs, draw in a host of evildoers, injure the enterprise of great peace, and lose the hopes of the four seas.

sentences.zh: 竊計陛下寧遠君子而不忍斥其徒，寧棄讜言而不欲違其教，亦謂可以延年已疾耳。

translations.literal: I privately reckon that Your Majesty would rather keep gentlemen at a distance than bear to dismiss these followers, and would rather discard honest counsel than go against their teaching, thinking that it can prolong life and cure illness.
translations.idiomatic: I privately reckon that Your Majesty would rather keep gentlemen at a distance than bear to dismiss these followers, and would rather discard honest counsel than go against their teaching, thinking that it can prolong life and cure illness.

sentences.zh: 側聞頃來嬪御女謁，充塞閨幃，一二黠慧柔曼者為惑尤甚。

translations.literal: I have heard on the side that recently palace women and sorceresses have filled the inner chambers, and one or two who are clever, soft, and beguiling have been especially corrupting.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that recently palace women and sorceresses have filled the inner chambers, and one or two who are clever, soft, and beguiling have been especially corrupting.

sentences.zh: 由是，怠日講，疏召對，政令多僻，起居愆度。

translations.literal: From this the daily lecture is neglected, summons for audience grow rare, government orders are often perverse, and daily conduct departs from proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: From this the daily lecture is neglected, summons for audience grow rare, government orders are often perverse, and daily conduct departs from proper measure.

sentences.zh: 小人窺見間隙，遂以左道蠱惑。

translations.literal: Petty men saw the openings and used heterodox ways to bewitch and delude.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men saw the openings and used heterodox ways to bewitch and delude.

sentences.zh: 夫以齋醮為足恃而恣欲宮壺之間，以荒淫為無傷而邀福邪妄之術，甚非古帝王求福不回之道也。」

translations.literal: To rely on fasting and offerings alone while indulging desires within the inner quarters, to treat debauchery as harmless and seek blessing through wicked and false arts—this is very far from the way ancient emperors and kings sought blessing without turning aside."
translations.idiomatic: To rely on fasting and offerings alone while indulging desires within the inner quarters, to treat debauchery as harmless and seek blessing through wicked and false arts—this is very far from the way ancient emperors and kings sought blessing without turning aside.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年四月，以災異，偕六科諸臣上疏曰：「昔成湯以六事自責曰：『政不節歟？

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Jiajing, because of omens and disasters, he joined the ministers of the six bureaus in submitting a memorial saying: "Formerly King Cheng Tang took six matters upon himself and said: 'Is government undisciplined?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Jiajing 2 (1523), because of omens and disasters, he joined the ministers of the six bureaus in submitting a memorial: "Formerly King Cheng Tang took six matters upon himself and said: 'Is government undisciplined?

sentences.zh: 民失職歟？

translations.literal: Have the people lost their livelihoods?
translations.idiomatic: Have the people lost their livelihoods?

sentences.zh: 宮壺崇歟？

translations.literal: Are the women of the inner quarters exalted?
translations.idiomatic: Are the women of the inner quarters exalted?

sentences.zh: 女謁盛歟？

translations.literal: Do sorceresses flourish?
translations.idiomatic: Do sorceresses flourish?

sentences.zh: 苞苴行歟？

translations.literal: Do bribes circulate?
translations.idiomatic: Do bribes circulate?

sentences.zh: 讒夫昌歟？』

translations.literal: Do slanderers prosper?
translations.idiomatic: Do slanderers prosper?

sentences.zh: 今誠以近事較之。

translations.literal: Now truly compare recent events with these.
translations.idiomatic: Now compare recent events with these.

sentences.zh: 快船方減而輒允戴保奏添，鎮戍方裁而更聽趙榮分守。

translations.literal: The fast boats had just been reduced, yet Dai Bao's memorial to add more was promptly approved; the frontier garrisons had just been cut back, yet Zhao Rong was again allowed to share the command.
translations.idiomatic: The fast boats had just been reduced, yet Dai Bao's memorial to add more was promptly approved; the frontier garrisons had just been cut back, yet Zhao Rong was again allowed to share the command.

sentences.zh: 詔核馬房矣，隨格於閻洪之一言；

translations.literal: An edict had ordered an audit of the horse stables, yet it was promptly blocked by a single word from Yan Hong;
translations.idiomatic: An edict had ordered an audit of the horse stables, yet a single word from Yan Hong promptly blocked it;

sentences.zh: 詔汰軍匠矣，尋奪於監門之群咻。

translations.literal: An edict had ordered a reduction of military artisans, yet soon the order was overturned by the clamor of the gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had ordered a cutback of military artisans, yet the gate guards' uproar soon overturned it.

sentences.zh: 是政不可謂節也。

translations.literal: Thus government cannot be said to be disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: Thus government cannot be called disciplined.

sentences.zh: 末作競於奇巧，遊手半於閭閻。

translations.literal: Secondary crafts compete in ingenious artifice, and idle hands fill half the lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary trades vie in ingenious artifice, and idle hands fill half the neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 耕桑時廢，缺俯仰之資；

translations.literal: Farming and sericulture are neglected at times, and people lack the means to sustain their daily living;
translations.idiomatic: Farming and sericulture are neglected, and people lack the means to sustain their daily living;

sentences.zh: 教化未聞，成偷薄之習。

translations.literal: Moral instruction is unheard of, and a habit of frivolity and petty roguery takes shape.
translations.idiomatic: Moral instruction goes unheard, and a habit of frivolity and petty roguery takes hold.

sentences.zh: 是民不可謂不失職也。

translations.literal: Thus the people cannot be said not to have lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people cannot be said to have kept their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 兩宮營建，采運艱辛。

translations.literal: Construction of the two palaces made timber procurement and transport grievously arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Construction of the two palaces made timber procurement and transport grievously arduous.

sentences.zh: 或一木而役夫萬千，或一椽而廢財十百。

translations.literal: For one log, ten thousand laborers might be impressed; for one rafter, a hundred or a thousand in wealth might be squandered.
translations.idiomatic: For a single log, ten thousand laborers might be impressed; for a single rafter, fortunes might be squandered.

sentences.zh: 死亡枕藉之狀，呻吟號嘆之聲，陛下不得而見聞。

translations.literal: The sight of the dead piled upon one another, the sound of moaning and wailing—Your Majesty cannot see or hear them.
translations.idiomatic: The dead lie piled upon one another; moans and cries of anguish fill the air—yet Your Majesty cannot see or hear them.

sentences.zh: 是宮壺不可謂不崇也。

translations.literal: Thus the inner palace cannot be said to be not exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the inner palace cannot be called anything but exalted.

sentences.zh: 奉聖、保聖之後，先女寵於冊後；

translations.literal: After the titles Fengsheng and Baosheng, concubines gained favor ahead of the empress;
translations.idiomatic: After the titles Fengsheng and Baosheng were granted, concubines won favor ahead of the empress;

sentences.zh: 莊奉、肅奉之名，聯殊稱於乳母。

translations.literal: The honorific titles Zhuangfeng and Sufeng linked extraordinary appellations to wet nurses.
translations.idiomatic: The honorific titles Zhuangfeng and Sufeng attached extraordinary appellations to wet nurses.

sentences.zh: 或承恩漸鄰於飛燕，或黠慧不下於婉兒。

translations.literal: Some in receiving favor nearly rivaled Zhao Feiyan; some in cleverness were no less than Wan'er.
translations.idiomatic: Some in imperial favor nearly rivaled Zhao Feiyan; some in wit were no less than Wan'er.

sentences.zh: 內以移主上之性情，外以開近習之負倚。

translations.literal: Within they shift the sovereign's temperament; without they open the way for favorites to lean on power.
translations.idiomatic: Within they shift the sovereign's temperament; without they open the way for favorites to lean on power.

sentences.zh: 是女謁不可謂不盛也。

translations.literal: Thus women with access to the throne cannot be said not to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Thus women with access to the throne cannot be called anything but flourishing.

sentences.zh: 窮奸之銳、雄，公肆賂遺而逃籍沒之律；

translations.literal: The utterly wicked Rui and Xiong openly bestowed bribes and gifts, evading the law of confiscation;
translations.idiomatic: The utterly wicked Zhang Rui and Zhang Xiong openly bestowed bribes and gifts, evading the law of confiscation;

sentences.zh: 極惡之鵬、鎧，密行請托而逋三載之誅。

translations.literal: The utterly depraved Peng and Kai secretly made entreaties and bribes, evading execution for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The utterly depraved Liao Peng and Liao Kai secretly made entreaties and bribes, evading execution for three years.

sentences.zh: 錢神靈而王英改問於錦衣，關節通而於喜竟漏於禁網。

translations.literal: The spirit of money worked its magic and Wang Ying's case was transferred to the Embroidered Uniform Guard; backdoor connections were opened and Yu Xi entirely slipped through the prohibition net.
translations.idiomatic: Money worked its magic and Wang Ying's case was transferred to the Embroidered Uniform Guard; backdoor connections were opened and Yu Xi entirely slipped through the legal net.

sentences.zh: 是苞苴不可謂不行也。

translations.literal: Thus bribes cannot be said not to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Thus bribes cannot be called anything but rampant.

sentences.zh: 獻廟主祀，屈府部之議，而用王槐諛佞之謀；

translations.literal: In offering at the ancestral temple, the deliberations of the ministries were overridden and Wang Huai's fawning and sycophantic scheme was adopted;
translations.idiomatic: In offerings at the ancestral temple, the ministries' deliberations were overridden and Wang Huai's fawning scheme was adopted;

sentences.zh: 重臣批答，乏體貌之宜，而入群小惎間之論。

translations.literal: When senior ministers issued reply memorials, they lacked proper dignity and fell into the talk of petty men sowing discord.
translations.idiomatic: When senior ministers issued reply memorials, they lacked proper dignity and fell into the talk of petty men sowing discord.

sentences.zh: 或譖發於內，陰肆毒螫；

translations.literal: Some slanders arose from within, secretly spreading poisonous stings;
translations.idiomatic: Some slanders arose from within, secretly spreading poisonous stings;

sentences.zh: 或讒行於外，顯逞擠排。

translations.literal: Some calumnies circulated without, openly wielding ostracism and expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Some calumnies circulated without, openly wielding ostracism and expulsion.

sentences.zh: 上以汨朝廷之是非，下以亂人物之邪正。

translations.literal: Above they muddy right and wrong at court; below they confound the distinction between the wicked and the upright among men.
translations.idiomatic: Above they muddy right and wrong at court; below they confound the distinction between the wicked and the upright.

sentences.zh: 是讒夫不可謂不昌也。

translations.literal: Thus slanderers cannot be said not to prosper.
translations.idiomatic: Thus slanderers cannot be called anything but flourishing.

sentences.zh: 凡此，皆成湯之所無，而今日之所有，是以不避斧鉞之誅，用附責難之義。

translations.literal: All these are faults that Cheng Tang did not have, yet the present day does—therefore I do not shun execution by axe and halberd, and append this charge of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: All these are faults Cheng Tang did not have, yet the present day does—therefore I do not shun execution by axe and halberd, and offer this remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 望陛下采納。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will accept and act on this."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will accept this."

sentences.zh: 其年冬，命中官督蘇、杭織造，舉朝阻之不能得。

translations.literal: That winter, the Emperor ordered eunuchs to supervise weaving in Suzhou and Hangzhou; the whole court opposed it but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Emperor ordered eunuchs to supervise weaving in Suzhou and Hangzhou; the whole court opposed it but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 翀復偕同官張原等力爭。

translations.literal: Chong again joined his colleague Zhang Yuan and others in pressing the issue forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Chong again joined his colleague Zhang Yuan and others in pressing the issue forcefully.

sentences.zh: 時世宗初政，楊廷和等在內閣。

translations.literal: At the time it was the beginning of the Shizong Emperor's reign, and Yang Tinghe and others were in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was the beginning of the Jiajing Emperor's reign, and Yang Tinghe and others served in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 群小雖已用事，正論猶伸，翀前後指斥無所避。

translations.literal: Though petty men were already wielding power, upright opinion still had sway, and Chong censured them front and back without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Though petty men were already wielding power, upright opinion still had sway, and Chong censured them without evasion.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不見用，然亦嘗報聞，不罪也。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor did not adopt his advice, he nevertheless sometimes acknowledged receipt and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Emperor did not adopt his advice, he sometimes acknowledged receipt and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 及明年三月，帝以桂萼言，銳欲考獻帝，且欲立廟禁中，翀復偕同官力諫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, on Gui E's advice the Emperor was keen to posthumously honor the Prince of Xing and also wished to erect a temple within the Forbidden City; Chong again joined his colleagues in forceful remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year, on Gui E's advice the Emperor was keen to posthumously honor his father, the Prince of Xing, and also wished to erect a temple within the Forbidden City; Chong again joined his colleagues in forceful remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝於是責以朋言亂政，命奪俸。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon rebuked them for factional talk disturbing government and ordered their salaries confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon rebuked them for factional talk disturbing government and ordered their salaries confiscated.

sentences.zh: 既又助尚書喬宇等再疏爭內殿建室之議，被詔切讓。

translations.literal: Then, supporting Minister Qiao Yu and others, he again memorialized against building halls in the inner palace, and was sharply reprimanded by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Then, supporting Minister Qiao Yu and others, he again memorialized against building halls in the inner palace and was sharply reprimanded by edict.

sentences.zh: 呂柟、鄒守益下獄，翀等抗疏救。

translations.literal: When Lü Zan and Zou Shouyi were imprisoned, Chong and others submitted urgent memorials in their defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Zan and Zou Shouyi were imprisoned, Chong and others submitted urgent memorials in their defense.

sentences.zh: 及張璁、桂萼召至，翀與給事三十余人連章言：「兩人賦性奸邪，立心憸佞，變亂宗廟，離間宮闈，詆毀詔書，中傷善類。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were summoned to court, Chong and more than thirty supervising secretaries submitted successive memorials saying: "The two men's natures are treacherous and wicked; their hearts are grasping and sycophantic; they would overturn the ancestral temples and sow discord within the palace, revile the imperial edicts, and strike at good men.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were summoned to court, Chong and more than thirty supervising secretaries submitted successive memorials: "The two men's natures are treacherous and wicked; their hearts are grasping and sycophantic; they would overturn the ancestral temples and sow discord within the palace, revile the imperial edicts, and strike at good men.

sentences.zh: 望亟出之，為人臣不忠之戒。」

translations.literal: We hope they will be expelled at once, as a warning to disloyal ministers."
translations.idiomatic: We hope they will be expelled at once, as a warning to disloyal ministers."

sentences.zh: 皆不納。

translations.literal: All was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: All was rejected.

sentences.zh: 帝愈欲考獻帝，改孝宗為伯考，翀等憂之。

translations.literal: The Emperor became all the more intent on honoring the Prince of Xing and redesignating Emperor Xiaozong as "Uncle-Father"; Chong and the others were deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor became all the more intent on honoring the Prince of Xing and redesignating Emperor Xiaozong as "Uncle-Father"; Chong and the others were deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 會給事中張漢卿劾席書振荒不法，戶部尚書秦金請命官往勘，帝是之。

translations.literal: When Supervising Secretary Zhang Hanqing impeached Xi Shu for lawless excess and irregular conduct, Minister of Revenue Qin Jin requested that officials be dispatched to investigate, and the Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Secretary Zhang Hanqing impeached Xi Shu for lawless excess, Minister of Revenue Qin Jin requested that officials be dispatched to investigate, and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 翀等乃取廷臣劾萼等章疏，送刑部令上請，且私相語曰：「倘上亦雲是者，即撲殺之。」

translations.literal: Chong and the others then took the court officials' memorials impeaching Gui E and others, sent them to the Ministry of Justice with a request to the throne, and privately said to one another: "If the Emperor also says yes, then strike them down at once."
translations.idiomatic: Chong and the others then took the court officials' memorials impeaching Gui E and others, sent them to the Ministry of Justice with a request to the throne, and privately said to one another: "If the Emperor also agrees, then strike them down at once."

sentences.zh: 璁等以其語聞。

translations.literal: Cong and the others reported their words to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and the others reported their words to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝留疏不下，而責刑部尚書趙鑒等朋邪害正，翀等陷義罔忠，而進璁、萼學士。

translations.literal: The Emperor kept the memorials without action but rebuked Minister of Justice Zhao Rong and others for factional wickedness harming the upright, and Chong and the others for betraying righteousness and deceiving loyalty—while advancing Cong and Gui E to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept the memorials without action but rebuked Minister of Justice Zhao Rong and others for factional wickedness harming the upright, and Chong and the others for betraying righteousness and deceiving loyalty—while advancing Cong and Gui E to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 廷臣相顧駭嘆。

translations.literal: The court officials looked at one another in alarm and lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials looked at one another in alarm and lamentation.

sentences.zh: 諸曹乃各具一疏，力言孝宗不可稱伯考，署名者凡二百二十余人。

translations.literal: The various bureaus then each submitted a memorial forcefully stating that Emperor Xiaozong could not be called "Uncle-Father"; those who signed numbered more than two hundred twenty in all.
translations.idiomatic: The various bureaus then each submitted a memorial forcefully stating that Emperor Xiaozong could not be called "Uncle-Father"; more than two hundred twenty officials signed.

sentences.zh: 帝皆留中不報。

translations.literal: The Emperor kept them all sealed in the palace without reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept them all sealed in the palace without reply.

sentences.zh: 七月戊寅，諸臣相率伏左順門懇請。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the seventh month, the ministers in a body prostrated themselves at the Left Shun Gate and earnestly petitioned.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the seventh month, the ministers in a body prostrated themselves at the Left Shun Gate and earnestly petitioned.

sentences.zh: 帝兩遣中官諭之不退，遂震怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor twice sent eunuchs to instruct them, but they would not withdraw; he then erupted in fury.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor twice sent eunuchs to instruct them, but they would not withdraw; he then erupted in fury.

sentences.zh: 先逮諸曹為首者八人於詔獄，翀與焉。

translations.literal: First he arrested the eight leading bureau heads in the imperial prison, Chong among them.
translations.idiomatic: First he arrested the eight leading bureau heads in the imperial prison, Chong among them.

sentences.zh: 尋杖於廷，謫戍瞿塘衛，而璁、萼寵益盛。

translations.literal: Soon they were beaten at court and exiled to Qutang Guard, while Cong and Gui E's favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they were beaten at court and exiled to Qutang Guard, while Cong and Gui E's favor grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 翀居戍所十余年，以東宮冊立恩放還，卒。

translations.literal: Chong remained at his place of exile for more than ten years; he was released through the grace granted when the crown prince was invested, and died soon after.
translations.idiomatic: Chong remained in exile for more than ten years; he was released through the grace granted when the crown prince was invested, and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，進刑科都給事中。

translations.literal: When the Jiajing reign title was adopted, he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing reign title was adopted, he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 主事陳嘉言坐事下獄，濟疏救，不許。

translations.literal: Section Chief Chen Jiayan was imprisoned for an offense; Ji memorialized in his defense, but permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Section Chief Chen Jiayan was imprisoned for an offense; Ji memorialized in his defense, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 廖鵬父子及錢寧黨王欽等，皆以從逆論斬，鵬等夤緣中人冀脫死。

translations.literal: Liao Peng, father and son, and Wang Qin and others, associates of Qian Ning's faction, were all sentenced to decapitation for following rebellion; Peng and the others used connections with eunuchs hoping to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Peng, father and son, and Wang Qin and others, associates of Qian Ning's faction, were all sentenced to decapitation for following rebellion; Peng and the others used connections with eunuchs hoping to escape death.

sentences.zh: 濟上言：「自來死囚臨斬，鼓下猶受訴詞。

translations.literal: Ji submitted a memorial: "From ancient times, when condemned prisoners faced execution, petitions were still accepted even after the execution drum sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Ji submitted a memorial: "From ancient times, when condemned prisoners faced execution, petitions were still accepted even after the execution drum sounded.

sentences.zh: 奏上得報，已及日旰，再請而後行刑，則已薄暮。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted and an answer received, it was already late in the day; only after a second request would execution proceed—and then it was already dusk.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted and an answer received, it was already late in the day; only after a second request would execution proceed—and then it was already dusk.

sentences.zh: 殊非與眾棄之之意。

translations.literal: This is quite contrary to the intent of having them cast off by the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: This is quite contrary to the intent of executing them with public approval.

sentences.zh: 乞自三請後，鼓下不得受詞。

translations.literal: I beg that after the third request, no words be accepted at the drum.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that after the third request, no petitions be accepted at the execution drum.

sentences.zh: 鵬、欽等罪甚當，幸陛下勿疑。」

translations.literal: Peng, Qin, and the others are fully deserving of their crimes; I hope Your Majesty will not doubt it."
translations.idiomatic: Peng, Qin, and the others fully deserve their sentences; I hope Your Majesty will not doubt it."

sentences.zh: 詔自今以申酉行刑，鵬等竟緩決。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from then on executions be carried out between the shen and you hours; Peng and the others were ultimately given suspended sentences.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that from then on executions be carried out between 3 and 7 p.m.; Peng and the others were ultimately given suspended sentences.

sentences.zh: 欽後以中旨免死。

translations.literal: Qin was later spared death by rescript from the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was later spared death by rescript from the inner court.

sentences.zh: 濟力爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Ji argued forcefully but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ji argued forcefully but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 故事，廠衛有所逮，必取原奏情事送刑科簽發駕帖。

translations.literal: By precedent, whenever the Depots or Guard made an arrest, the original memorial on the facts had to be sent to the Bureau of Punishments for countersignature on the arrest warrant.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, whenever the Depots or Guard made an arrest, the original memorial on the facts had to be sent to the Bureau of Punishments for countersignature on the arrest warrant.

sentences.zh: 千戶白壽賫帖至，濟索原奏，壽不與，濟亦不肯簽發。

translations.literal: When Thousand-Commander Bai Shou arrived with the warrant, Ji demanded the original memorial; Shou would not provide it, and Ji likewise refused to countersign.
translations.idiomatic: When Thousand-Commander Bai Shou arrived with the warrant, Ji demanded the original memorial; Shou would not provide it, and Ji likewise refused to countersign.

sentences.zh: 兩人列詞上。

translations.literal: Both submitted statements to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Both submitted statements to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝先入壽言，竟詘濟議。

translations.literal: The Emperor, swayed first by Shou's account, ultimately rejected Ji's position.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, swayed first by Shou's account, ultimately rejected Ji's position.

sentences.zh: 中官崔文仆李陽鳳坐罪，已下刑部。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Cui Wen and Li Yangfeng had been convicted and already sent to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Cui Wen and Li Yangfeng had been convicted and already sent to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝受文訴，移之鎮撫。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted Wen's appeal and transferred the case to the Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted Wen's appeal and transferred the case to the Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 濟率六科爭之，不聽。

translations.literal: Ji led the Six Bureaus in protesting; they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ji led the Six Bureaus in protesting; they were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 都督劉暉以奸黨論戍，有詔復官。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief Liu Hui had been sentenced to exile as a treacherous factionalist; an edict restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Liu Hui had been sentenced to exile as a treacherous factionalist; an edict restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 甘肅總兵官李隆嗾亂軍殺巡撫許銘，逮入都，營免赴鞫。

translations.literal: The Gansu regional commander Li Long incited mutinous troops to kill Grand Coordinator Xu Ming; after Li was brought to the capital, he worked to avoid being sent for trial.
translations.idiomatic: The Gansu regional commander Li Long incited mutinous troops to kill Grand Coordinator Xu Ming; after Li was brought to the capital, he worked to avoid being sent for trial.

sentences.zh: 濟皆力陳不可，帝從其言。

translations.literal: Ji forcefully stated in each case that this could not be allowed, and the Emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Ji forcefully stated in each case that this could not be allowed, and the Emperor accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 暉奪職，隆受訊伏辜。

translations.literal: Hui was stripped of office; Long was interrogated and paid the penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was stripped of office; Long was interrogated and paid the penalty.

sentences.zh: 定國公徐光祚規占民田，嗾灤州民訐前永平知府郭九臯。

translations.literal: Duke of Dingguo Xu Guangzuo encroached on commoners' fields, inciting Luanzhou people to accuse the former Yongping prefect Guo Jiugao.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Dingguo Xu Guangzuo encroached on commoners' fields, inciting Luanzhou people to accuse the former Yongping prefect Guo Jiugao.

sentences.zh: 太監芮景賢主之，緹騎逮訊。

translations.literal: Eunuch Rui Jingxian directed the matter, and mounted guards arrested and interrogated them.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Rui Jingxian directed the matter, and mounted guards arrested and interrogated them.

sentences.zh: 濟請並治光祚，章下所司。

translations.literal: Ji requested that Guangzuo be punished as well; the memorial was sent down to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Ji requested that Guangzuo be punished as well; the memorial was sent down to the responsible office.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉最以劾中官崔文調外任，景賢復劾其違禁，與御史黃國用皆逮下詔獄，戍最而謫國用。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Zui was transferred to an outer post for impeaching eunuch Cui Wen; Jingxian again impeached him for violating prohibitions, and both Liu and Censor Huang Guoyong were arrested and sent to the imperial prison—Liu was exiled and Huang was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Zui was transferred to an outer post for impeaching eunuch Cui Wen; Jingxian again impeached him for violating prohibitions, and both Liu and Censor Huang Guoyong were arrested and sent to the imperial prison—Liu was exiled and Huang was demoted.

sentences.zh: 法司爭不得，濟言：「國家置三法司，專理刑獄，或主質成，或主平反。

translations.literal: The judicial offices protested without success; Ji said: "The state established the Three Judicial Offices specifically to handle criminal cases—some to verify judgments, some to reverse wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices protested without success; Ji said: "The state established the Three Judicial Offices specifically to handle criminal cases—some to verify judgments, some to reverse wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 權臣不得以恩怨為出入，天子不得以喜怒為重輕。

translations.literal: Powerful officials must not decide cases by private grudges, nor may the Son of Heaven weigh guilt by personal pleasure or anger.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful officials must not decide cases by private grudges, nor may the Son of Heaven weigh guilt by personal pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 自錦衣鎮撫之官專理詔獄，而法司幾成虛設。

translations.literal: Since the Embroidered Uniform and Brocade Guards alone have handled imperial prison cases, the judicial offices have nearly become a hollow institution.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Embroidered Uniform and Brocade Guards alone have handled imperial prison cases, the judicial offices have nearly become a hollow institution.

sentences.zh: 如最等小過耳，羅織於告密之門，鍛煉於詔獄之手。

translations.literal: A petty fault like Liu's and the others' becomes a pretext framed through the channels of informers and forged in the hands of the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Petty faults like Liu's become pretexts framed through the channels of informers and forged in the hands of the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 旨從內降，大臣初不與知，為聖政累非淺。

translations.literal: Rescripts descend from within; great ministers learn of them only afterward—this does no small harm to sagely government.
translations.idiomatic: Rescripts descend from within; great ministers learn of them only afterward—this does no small harm to sagely government.

sentences.zh: 且李洪、陳宣罪至殺人，降級而已。

translations.literal: Moreover Li Hong and Chen Xuan committed crimes reaching murder, yet received only demotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Li Hong and Chen Xuan committed crimes reaching murder, yet received only demotion in rank.

sentences.zh: 王欽兄弟黨奸亂政，謫戍而已。

translations.literal: Wang Qin and his brothers, partisans who joined with wicked men to disturb government, received only exile.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qin and his brothers, partisans who joined with wicked men to disturb government, received only exile.

sentences.zh: 以最等視之，奚啻天淵，而罪顧一律，何以示天下？」

translations.literal: Compared with men like Liu, the difference is more than heaven from abyss—yet the crimes are treated the same. How is the empire to be shown?"
translations.idiomatic: Compared with men like Liu, the difference is more than heaven from abyss—yet the punishments are treated the same. How is this to be shown to the empire?"

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪濟俸一月。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and confiscated Ji's salary for one month.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry and confiscated Ji's salary for one month.

sentences.zh: 後父陳萬言奴何璽毆人死，帝命釋之。
