translations.literal: The empress's father Chen Wanyan's slave He Xi beat a man to death; the Emperor ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father Chen Wanyan's slave He Xi beat a man to death; the Emperor ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 濟執奏曰：「萬言縱奴殺人，得免為幸，乃並釋璽等，是法不行於戚畹奴也。」

translations.literal: Ji submitted a firm memorial: "Wanyan indulged his slave in murder and might count himself fortunate to be spared—yet Xi and the others are also released. This means the law does not run to the slaves of imperial in-laws."
translations.idiomatic: Ji submitted a firm memorial: "Wanyan indulged his slave in murder and might count himself fortunate to be spared—yet Xi and the others are also released. This means the law does not run to the slaves of imperial in-laws."

sentences.zh: 濟在諫垣久，言論侃侃，多與權幸相枝柱，直聲甚震，帝滋不能堪。

translations.literal: Ji had long served in the remonstrance offices; his words were forceful and forthright, and he often clashed with the powerful and favored—his reputation for integrity resounded, and the Emperor grew ever less able to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had long served in the remonstrance offices; his words were forceful and forthright, and he often clashed with the powerful and favored—his reputation for integrity resounded, and the Emperor grew ever less able to bear it.

sentences.zh: 「大禮」議起，廷臣爭者多得罪。

translations.literal: When the "Grand Rites" controversy arose, many who remonstrated at court were punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the "Grand Rites" controversy arose, many who remonstrated at court were punished.

sentences.zh: 濟疏救修撰呂柟，編修鄒守益，給事中鄧繼曾，御史馬明衡、朱淛、陳逅、季本，郎中林應驄，不聽。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized in defense of Compiler Lü Zan, Compiler Zou Shouyi, Supervising Secretary Deng Jiceng, Censors Ma Mingheng, Zhu Beng, Chen Hui, and Ji Ben, and Section Chief Lin Yinglin—but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ji memorialized in defense of Compiler Lü Zan, Compiler Zou Shouyi, Supervising Secretary Deng Jiceng, Censors Ma Mingheng, Zhu Beng, Chen Hui, and Ji Ben, and Section Chief Lin Yinglin—but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 既而遮諸朝臣於金水橋，伏哭左順門，受杖闕廷。

translations.literal: Later he joined other court officials at the Golden Water Bridge, prostrated himself, and wept at the Left Shun Gate, and was beaten at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined other court officials at the Golden Water Bridge, prostrated himself, and wept at the Left Shun Gate, and was beaten at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 越十二日再杖，謫戍遼東。

translations.literal: Twelve days later he was beaten again and exiled to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve days later he was beaten again and exiled to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 十六年冊立皇太子，赦諸謫戍者，濟不與，卒於戍所。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when the crown prince was invested, all exiles were pardoned—Ji was not included, and he died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when the crown prince was invested, all exiles were pardoned—Ji was not included, and he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初復官，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the early Longqing reign his office was posthumously restored, and he was granted the title Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Longqing reign his office was posthumously restored, and he was granted the title Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 安磐，字公石，嘉定州人。

translations.literal: An Pan, styled Gongshi, was a native of Jiading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An Pan, styled Gongshi, was a native of Jiading Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 18 (1505).

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as a Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 正德時，歷吏、兵二科給事中，乞假去。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign, he served successively as Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of Personnel and in the Scrutiny of War, then requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he served in succession as Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of Personnel and the Scrutiny of War, then requested leave and left office.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，起故官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔欲加興獻帝皇號，磐言：「興，藩國也，不可加於帝號之上。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued a personal edict wishing to add the imperial title to the Prince of Xingxian; Pan said: "Xing is a fief designation and cannot be placed above an imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued a personal edict wishing to add an imperial title to the Prince of Xingxian; Pan said: "'Xing' is a fief designation and cannot be placed above an imperial title.

sentences.zh: 獻，謚法也，不可加於生存之母。

translations.literal: Xian is a posthumous name and cannot be applied to a living mother.
translations.idiomatic: 'Xian' is a posthumous name and cannot be applied to a living mother.

sentences.zh: 本生、所後，勢不俱尊。

translations.literal: The biological parent and the adoptive parent cannot both be honored at the same level.
translations.idiomatic: One's biological parent and adoptive parent cannot both be honored equally.

sentences.zh: 大義私恩，自有輕重。」

translations.literal: Public duty and private gratitude have their own order of priority."
translations.idiomatic: Public duty and private gratitude each have their proper weight."

sentences.zh: 會廷臣多力爭，事得且止。

translations.literal: At that time many court officials forcefully remonstrated, and the matter was halted for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many court officials remonstrated forcefully, and the matter was halted for the time being.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，主事霍韜言，科道官褻服受詔，大不敬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, Section Chief Huo Tao reported that censorate officials had received the edict in disrespectful attire—an enormous breach of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 (1522), Section Chief Huo Tao reported that censorate officials had received the edict in informal dress—a grave breach of propriety.

sentences.zh: 磐偕同官論韜先以議禮得罪名教，恐言官發其奸，故摭拾細事，意在傾排。

translations.literal: Pan joined his colleagues in arguing that Huo had first offended moral orthodoxy in the Rites controversy and, fearing that remonstrance officials would expose his wrongdoing, was dredging up petty matters with the intent of destroying and expelling them.
translations.idiomatic: Pan joined his colleagues in arguing that Huo had first offended moral orthodoxy in the Rites controversy and, fearing that remonstrance officials would expose his wrongdoing, was dredging up petty matters in order to destroy and expel them.

sentences.zh: 帝置不問。

translations.literal: The Emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 尋因事言：「先朝內外巨奸，若張忠、劉養、韋霦、魏彬、王瓊、寧杲等，漏網得全要領。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on another matter, he said: "The great villains of the previous reign, inside and outside the court—men such as Zhang Zhong, Liu Yang, Wei Bang, Wei Bin, Wang Qiong, and Ning Gao—slipped through the net and kept their necks intact.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on another matter, he said: "The great villains of the previous reign, inside and outside the court—men such as Zhang Zhong, Liu Yang, Wei Bang, Wei Bin, Wang Qiong, and Ning Gao—slipped through the net and kept their heads.

sentences.zh: 其貨賂可以通神，未嘗不夤緣覬復用。

translations.literal: Their bribes can move heaven itself; they never stop climbing by connections in hope of being employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Their bribes can move heaven itself; they never stop using connections in hope of being employed again.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴察預防，天下事毋令若輩再壞。」

translations.literal: We should scrutinize them strictly and guard against them in advance, lest such men ruin the affairs of the empire once more."
translations.idiomatic: They should be scrutinized strictly and guarded against in advance, lest such men ruin the empire again."

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，命錦衣官密訪緝之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his counsel and ordered Embroidered Uniform Guard officers to investigate and apprehend them in secret.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his counsel and ordered Embroidered Uniform Guard officers to investigate and apprehend them in secret.

sentences.zh: 中官張欽家人李賢者，帝許任為錦衣指揮。

translations.literal: Li Xian, a servant in the household of the eunuch Zhang Qin, was permitted by the Emperor to be appointed a commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, a servant in the household of the eunuch Zhang Qin, was permitted by the Emperor to be appointed a commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 磐極言不可，不聽。

translations.literal: Pan spoke forcefully against this, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Pan spoke forcefully against this, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 錦衣千戶張儀以附中官張銳黜革，御史楊百之忽為訟冤，言；

translations.literal: Chief Zhang Yi of the Embroidered Uniform Guard had been dismissed for siding with the eunuch Zhang Rui; suddenly Censor Yang Baizhi petitioned in his defense, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chief Zhang Yi of the Embroidered Uniform Guard had been dismissed for siding with the eunuch Zhang Rui; suddenly Censor Yang Baizhi petitioned in his defense, saying:

sentences.zh: 「儀當宸濠逆謀時，首倡大義，勸銳卻其饋遺。

translations.literal: "When Prince Ning's rebellion was afoot, Yi was the first to uphold the great cause and urged Rui to refuse his bribes.
translations.idiomatic: "When Prince Ning's rebellion was afoot, Yi was the first to uphold the righteous cause and urged Rui to refuse his bribes.

sentences.zh: 今銳以是免死，儀功不錄，無以示報。」

translations.literal: Now Rui was spared death on that account, yet Yi's merit went unrewarded—there is no way to show recompense."
translations.idiomatic: Now Rui was spared death on that account, yet Yi's merit went unrewarded—there is no way to show proper recompense."

sentences.zh: 磐疏言：「百之憸邪，陽為儀遊說，而陰與銳交關，為銳再起地。」

translations.literal: Pan memorialized: "Baizhi is treacherous and base; outwardly he pleads for Yi, while secretly he has dealings with Rui, paving the way for Rui's restoration."
translations.idiomatic: Pan memorialized: "Baizhi is treacherous and base; outwardly he pleads for Yi, while secretly he has dealings with Rui, paving the way for Rui's restoration."

sentences.zh: 百之情得，乃誣磐因請屬不行，挾私行謗。

translations.literal: Baizhi's stratagem was exposed, whereupon he accused Pan of having solicited favor on his behalf and, when refused, of slandering him from private malice.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhi's stratagem was exposed, whereupon he accused Pan of having solicited favor on his behalf and, when refused, of slandering him out of private malice.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書喬宇等議黜百之，刑部謂情狀未明，宜俱逮治。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Qiao Yu and others recommended dismissing Baizhi; the Ministry of Justice held that the facts were unclear and that both men should be arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Qiao Yu and others recommended dismissing Baizhi; the Ministry of Justice held that the facts were unclear and that both men should be arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 帝兩宥之，奪百之俸三月，磐一月。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned them both, stripping Baizhi of three months' salary and Pan of one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned them both, stripping Baizhi of three months' salary and Pan of one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 帝頻興齋醮，磐又抗言：「曩武宗為左右所蠱，命番僧鎖南綽吉出入豹房，內官劉允迎佛西域。

translations.literal: The Emperor frequently held fasting rites and Daoist services; Pan remonstrated again: "Formerly Emperor Wuzong was deluded by those around him: he had the Tibetan monk Suonan Namgyal come and go in the Leopard Quarters, and the eunuch Liu Yun brought Buddhist images from the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor frequently held fasting rites and Daoist services; Pan remonstrated again: "Formerly Emperor Wuzong was deluded by those around him: he had the Tibetan monk Suonan Namgyal come and go in the Leopard Quarters, and the eunuch Liu Yun brought Buddhist images from the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 十數年間糜費大官，流謗道路。

translations.literal: For more than ten years the state treasury was squandered, and scandal spread along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years the state treasury was squandered, and scandal spread throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 自劉允放，而鎖南囚，供億減，小人伏。

translations.literal: After Liu Yun was dismissed and Suonan imprisoned, state expenses fell and petty men kept their heads down.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yun was dismissed and Suonan imprisoned, state expenses fell and petty men kept their heads down.

sentences.zh: 奈何甫及二年，遽襲舊轍。

translations.literal: Why, barely two years later, copy the old course so hastily?
translations.idiomatic: Why, barely two years into the new reign, follow the old course so hastily?

sentences.zh: 不齋則醮，月無虛日。

translations.literal: When not observing abstinence, you perform rites—and not a month passes without such a day.
translations.idiomatic: When not fasting, you hold rites—and not a month passes without such a day.

sentences.zh: 此豈陛下本意？

translations.literal: Can this truly be Your Majesty's own intent?
translations.idiomatic: Can this truly be Your Majesty's own intent?

sentences.zh: 實太監崔文等為之。

translations.literal: In fact the eunuchs Cui Wen and others have done this.
translations.idiomatic: In fact the eunuchs Cui Wen and others have done this.

sentences.zh: 文鐘鼓廝役，夤緣冒遷，既經降革，乃營求還職。

translations.literal: Wen was originally a menial in the bell-and-drum service; by connections he usurped promotion, and though once demoted and dismissed, he now schemes to regain his post.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was originally a menial in the bell-and-drum service; by connections he usurped promotion, and though once demoted and dismissed, he now schemes to regain his post.

sentences.zh: 導陛下至此，使貽譏天下後世，文可斬也。

translations.literal: Having led Your Majesty to this point and brought reproach on you before the empire and posterity, Wen deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: Having led Your Majesty to this point and brought reproach upon you before the empire and posterity, Wen deserves execution.

sentences.zh: 文嘗試陛下，欲行香則從之，欲登壇則從之，欲拜疏則又從之。

translations.literal: Wen has repeatedly tested Your Majesty: when he wanted incense offered, you complied; when he wanted to ascend the altar, you complied; when he wanted memorials submitted in ritual form, you complied again.
translations.idiomatic: Wen has repeatedly tested Your Majesty: when he wanted incense offered, you complied; when he wanted to ascend the altar, you complied; when he wanted memorials submitted in ritual form, you complied again.

sentences.zh: 無已則導以遊幸、土木，導以征伐，方且連類以進，伺便以逞。

translations.literal: If that were not enough, he would guide you toward tours and building projects, or toward military campaigns—and only then, gathering his kind, he would advance together and seize his opportunity to have his way.
translations.idiomatic: If that were not enough, he would guide you toward tours and building projects, or toward military campaigns—and only then, gathering his kind, would he advance together and seize his opportunity to have his way.

sentences.zh: 臣故曰文可斬也。」

translations.literal: Your subject therefore repeats: Wen deserves execution."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject therefore repeats: Wen deserves execution."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.

sentences.zh: 戶部主事羅洪載以杖錦衣百戶張瑾下詔獄，磐與同官張漢卿、張逵、葛鴊等請付之法司。

translations.literal: When Revenue Section Chief Luo Hongzai beat Embroidered Uniform Guard Centennial Zhang Jin and had him sent to the imperial prison, Pan joined his colleagues Zhang Hanqing, Zhang Kui, Ge Yan, and others in asking that the case be handed to the regular judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Revenue Section Chief Luo Hongzai beat Embroidered Uniform Guard Centennial Zhang Jin and had him sent to the imperial prison, Pan joined his colleagues Zhang Hanqing, Zhang Kui, Ge Yan, and others in asking that the case be handed to the regular judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 永福長公主下嫁，擇昏於七月下旬。

translations.literal: When the Princess of Yongfu was to marry, the wedding was set for late July.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess of Yongfu was to marry, the wedding was set for late July.

sentences.zh: 磐言：「長公主於孝惠皇太后為在室孫女，期服未滿，宜更其期。

translations.literal: Pan said: "The princess is an unmarried granddaughter to Empress Dowager Xiaohui; her one-year mourning period has not yet ended—the date ought to be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Pan said: "The princess is an unmarried granddaughter of Empress Dowager Xiaohui; her one-year mourning period has not yet ended—the date ought to be changed.

sentences.zh: 舊儀，駙馬見公主行兩拜禮，公主坐受。

translations.literal: By old ceremony the consort performed two bows upon meeting the princess, while the princess remained seated to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: By old ceremony the consort performed two bows upon meeting the princess, while the princess remained seated to receive them.

sentences.zh: 乖夫婦之分，亦當革正。」

translations.literal: This violates the proper relation between husband and wife and should likewise be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: This violates the proper relation between husband and wife and should likewise be corrected."

sentences.zh: 帝以遺旨格之，相見禮如故。

translations.literal: The Emperor blocked this with a testamentary instruction, and the meeting ceremony remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor blocked this with a testamentary instruction, and the meeting ceremony remained as before.

sentences.zh: 錦衣革職旗校王邦奇屢乞復職，磐言：「邦奇等在正德世，貪饕搏噬，有若虎狼。

translations.literal: Dismissed bannerman Wang Bangqi of the Embroidered Uniform Guard repeatedly petitioned for reinstatement; Pan said: "Bangqi and others in the Zhengde era were ravenous and predatory, like tigers and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed bannerman Wang Bangqi of the Embroidered Uniform Guard repeatedly petitioned for reinstatement; Pan said: "Bangqi and others in the Zhengde era were ravenous and predatory, like tigers and wolves.

sentences.zh: 其捕奸盜也，或以一人而牽十余人，或以一家而連數十家，鍛煉獄詞，付之司寇，謂之『鑄銅板』。

translations.literal: When they hunted traitors and thieves, one man might implicate more than ten, or one household might drag in dozens of families; they forged testimony in prison and handed cases to the Ministry of Justice—this they called 'casting the copper plate.'
translations.idiomatic: When they hunted traitors and thieves, one man might implicate more than ten, or one household might drag in dozens of families; they forged testimony in prison and handed cases to the Ministry of Justice—this they called 'casting the copper plate.'

sentences.zh: 其緝妖言也，或用番役四出搜愚民詭異之書，或購奸僧潛行誘愚民彌勒之教，然後從而掩之，無有解脫，謂之『種妖言』。

translations.literal: When they hunted seditious speech, they might send foreign agents in all directions to search out books of strange doctrine among the simple folk, or hire wicked monks to go secretly and lure the ignorant into the Maitreya cult—then swoop down on them with no escape; this they called 'planting seditious talk.'
translations.idiomatic: When they hunted seditious speech, they might send foreign agents in all directions to search out books of strange doctrine among the common people, or hire wicked monks to go secretly and lure the ignorant into the Maitreya cult—then swoop down on them with no escape; this they called 'planting seditious talk.'

sentences.zh: 數十年內，死者填獄，生者冤號。

translations.literal: Within decades the dead filled the prisons and the living cried out in injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Within decades the dead filled the prisons and the living cried out in injustice.

sentences.zh: 今不追正其罪，使得保首領，亦已幸矣，尚敢肆然無忌，屢瀆天聽，何為者哉且陛下收已渙之人心，奠將危之國脈，實在登極一詔。

translations.literal: Now, without revisiting their crimes, they are allowed to keep their heads—that is already fortunate—yet they dare to act with brazen impunity and repeatedly disturb the imperial ear; what is their purpose? Moreover, Your Majesty gathered hearts already scattered and steadied a dynasty on the brink of collapse—all through the accession proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Now, without revisiting their crimes, they are allowed to keep their heads—that is already fortunate—yet they dare to act with brazen impunity and repeatedly disturb the imperial ear; what is their purpose? Moreover, Your Majesty gathered hearts already scattered and steadied a dynasty on the brink of collapse—all through the accession proclamation.

sentences.zh: 若使此輩攘臂，一朝壞之，則奸人環立蜂起，堤防潰決，不知所紀極矣。

translations.literal: If these men are allowed to raise their arms and ruin it overnight, wicked men will swarm up all around, the dikes will burst, and there will be no knowing where it ends.
translations.idiomatic: If these men are allowed to raise their arms and ruin it overnight, wicked men will swarm up all around, the dikes will burst, and there will be no knowing where it ends.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴究治，絕禍源。」

translations.literal: They should be rigorously investigated and punished, cutting off the source of disaster."
translations.idiomatic: They should be rigorously investigated and punished, cutting off the source of disaster."

sentences.zh: 帝不能從。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor could not agree.

sentences.zh: 其後邦奇卒為大厲，如磐言。

translations.literal: Later Bangqi did indeed become a great scourge, just as Pan had warned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bangqi did indeed become a great scourge, just as Pan had warned.

sentences.zh: 帝驛召席書、桂萼等，磐請斥之以謝天下，且言：「今欲別立一廟於大內，是明知恭穆不可入太廟矣。

translations.literal: When the Emperor summoned Xi Shu, Gui E, and others by courier, Pan asked that they be dismissed to appease the empire, and said further: "Now you wish to establish a separate shrine within the Inner Palace—this shows you already know that Gongmu cannot enter the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor summoned Xi Shu, Gui E, and others by courier, Pan asked that they be dismissed to appease the empire, and said further: "Now you wish to establish a separate shrine within the Inner Palace—this shows you already know that Gongmu cannot enter the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 夫孝宗既不得考，恭穆又不得入，是無考也。

translations.literal: If Emperor Xiaozong cannot be honored as father and Gongmu cannot enter the temple, you have no father to honor.
translations.idiomatic: If Emperor Xiaozong cannot be honored as father and Gongmu cannot enter the temple, you have no father to honor.

sentences.zh: 世豈有無考之太廟哉。

translations.literal: In all the world can there be an Imperial Ancestral Temple with no father to honor?
translations.idiomatic: In all the world can there be an Imperial Ancestral Temple with no father to honor?

sentences.zh: 此其說之自相矛盾者也。」

translations.literal: This is where their argument contradicts itself."
translations.idiomatic: This is where their argument contradicts itself."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 歷兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: He served as Chief Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chief Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of War.

sentences.zh: 以率眾伏闕再受杖，除名為民。

translations.literal: For leading the crowd in prostrating at the palace gate he was beaten twice and dismissed from office to become a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: For leading the crowd in prostrating at the palace gate he was beaten twice and dismissed from office, reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 張漢卿，字元傑，儀封人。

translations.literal: Zhang Hanqing, styled Yuanjie, was a native of Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hanqing, styled Yuanjie, was a native of Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Zhengde 6 (1511).

sentences.zh: 授魏縣知縣，征拜刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Wei County, then summoned and appointed Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Wei County, then summoned and appointed Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 嘗陳杜僥幸、廣儲積、慎刑獄三事，深切時弊。

translations.literal: He once presented three matters—checking opportunism, expanding stored reserves, and exercising care in criminal cases—cutting deeply into the afflictions of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented three matters—checking opportunism, expanding stored reserves, and exercising care in criminal cases—cutting deeply into the afflictions of the age.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 武宗將南巡，偕同官伏闕諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong planned a southern tour, he joined his colleagues in prostrating at the palace gate to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong planned a southern tour, he joined his colleagues in prostrating at the palace gate to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，從巡撫李鐸言，發帑金二十萬優恤宣府軍民。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, following Grand Coordinator Li Duo, two hundred thousand taels of silver from the treasury were disbursed to give preferential relief to soldiers and civilians in Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, following Grand Coordinator Li Duo's recommendation, two hundred thousand taels of silver from the treasury were disbursed to give preferential relief to soldiers and civilians in Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 以漢卿言，並發十三萬於大同。

translations.literal: On Hanqing's recommendation, another one hundred thirty thousand taels were also sent to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: On Hanqing's recommendation, another one hundred thirty thousand taels were also sent to Datong.

sentences.zh: 屢遷戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年冬，與同官上言：「陛下軫念畿輔莊田之害，遣官會勘。

translations.literal: In the winter of Jiajing 1, he joined his colleagues in memorializing: "Your Majesty, moved by the harm of estates in the capital region, dispatched officials for a joint survey.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jiajing 1 (1522), he joined his colleagues in memorializing: "Your Majesty, moved by the harm of estates in the capital region, dispatched officials for a joint survey.

sentences.zh: 敕自正德以後投獻及額外侵占者，盡以給民。

translations.literal: An edict declared that from Zhengde onward all offerings and extra encroachments should be entirely returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that from Zhengde onward all offerings and extra encroachments should be entirely returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 王言一布，天下孰不誦陛下之仁！

translations.literal: Once the royal word was promulgated, who in the empire did not proclaim Your Majesty's benevolence!
translations.idiomatic: Once the royal word was promulgated, who in the empire did not proclaim Your Majesty's benevolence!

sentences.zh: 乃者給事中夏言、御史樊繼祖、主事張希尹勘上涿州薰皮廠、安州鷹房草場，詔旨留用。

translations.literal: Yet when Supervising Secretary Xia Yan, Censor Fan Jizu, and Section Chief Zhang Xiyin surveyed the tannery at Zhuozhou and the hawking grounds at Anzhou, an edict ordered them retained for use.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Supervising Secretary Xia Yan, Censor Fan Jizu, and Section Chief Zhang Xiyin surveyed the tannery at Zhuozhou and the hawking grounds at Anzhou, an edict ordered them retained for use.

sentences.zh: 所司執奏，迄不肯從，非所以全大信昭至公也。

translations.literal: The responsible offices submitted firm memorials but were never obeyed—this is no way to preserve great trust and display the utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices submitted firm memorials but were never obeyed—this is no way to preserve great trust and display the utmost fairness.

sentences.zh: 皮廠起於馬永成，鷹房創於谷大用，皆奪民業為之。

translations.literal: The tannery arose under Ma Yongcheng and the hawking grounds under Gu Dayong—both were built by seizing the people's livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The tannery arose under Ma Yongcheng and the hawking grounds under Gu Dayong—both were built by seizing the people's livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 今馬俊、趙霦恃藩邸舊恩，妄求免革，是復蹈永成、大用故轍也。

translations.literal: Now Ma Jun and Zhao Bang, relying on old favor from the princely residence, rashly seek exemption from abolition—this is treading the old path of Yongcheng and Dayong again.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ma Jun and Zhao Bang, relying on old favor from the princely residence, rashly seek exemption from abolition—this is treading the old path of Yongcheng and Dayong again.

sentences.zh: 乞盡還之民，而嚴罪俊、霦，為欺罔者戒。」

translations.literal: We beg that all be fully returned to the people, and that Jun and Bang be sternly punished as a warning to deceivers."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that all be fully returned to the people, and that Jun and Bang be sternly punished as a warning to deceivers."

sentences.zh: 後父陳萬言請營新第，既又乞莊田，內官吳勛等請督蘇州織造，漢卿皆極諫。

translations.literal: Later the empress's father Chen Wanyan asked to build a new mansion and then sought estates; the eunuchs Wu Xun and others asked to supervise Suzhou silk weaving—Hanqing remonstrated forcefully against all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Later the empress's father Chen Wanyan asked to build a new mansion and then sought estates; the eunuchs Wu Xun and others asked to supervise Suzhou silk weaving—Hanqing remonstrated forcefully against all of this.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: His advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 應天諸府大旱，帝將鬻淮、浙余鹽及所沒產，易銀振之。

translations.literal: When the prefectures of Yingtian suffered severe drought, the Emperor planned to sell surplus salt from Huai and Zhe and confiscated property, exchanging them for silver for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefectures of Yingtian suffered severe drought, the Emperor planned to sell surplus salt from Huai and Zhe and confiscated property, exchanging them for silver for relief.

sentences.zh: 漢卿言：「易銀緩，非發帑金不可。」

translations.literal: Hanqing said: "Converting to silver would be slow; nothing but disbursing silver from the treasury will do."
translations.idiomatic: Hanqing said: "Converting to silver would be slow; nothing but disbursing silver from the treasury will do."

sentences.zh: 帝為發銀十五萬。

translations.literal: The Emperor released one hundred fifty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor released one hundred fifty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復偕同官言：「今天下一歲之供，不給一歲之用，加以水旱頻仍，物力殫屈。

translations.literal: Before long he again joined his colleagues in saying: "Today the empire's yearly revenue cannot meet a year's expenditure; added to this are frequent floods and droughts, and material resources are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again joined his colleagues in saying: "Today the empire's yearly revenue cannot meet a year's expenditure; added to this are frequent floods and droughts, and material resources are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 陛下方躬行節儉，而中官梁棟等奏營造缺珠寶，是欲括戶部之銀也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is personally practicing frugality, yet the eunuchs Liang Dong and others report that construction lacks jewels and pearls—this is a scheme to squeeze silver from the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is personally practicing frugality, yet the eunuchs Liang Dong and others report that construction lacks jewels and pearls—this is a scheme to squeeze silver from the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 梁政等又以蠲免三分之數，欲行京倉撥補，是欲耗太倉之粟也。

translations.literal: Liang Zheng and others also want to offset the amount waived by the one-third tax reduction by drawing from capital granaries—this is a scheme to drain the Grand Canal granary.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zheng and others also want to offset the amount waived by the one-third tax reduction by drawing from capital granaries—this is a scheme to drain the Grand Canal granary.

sentences.zh: 夫內庫不足，取之計部；

translations.literal: When the inner treasury falls short, they take from the Ministry of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: When the inner treasury falls short, they take from the Ministry of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 計部不足，取之郡邑小民。

translations.literal: when the Ministry of Revenue falls short, they take from county magistrates and the common people.
translations.idiomatic: when the Ministry of Revenue falls short, they take from county magistrates and the common people.

sentences.zh: 郡邑小民將安取哉？

translations.literal: When county magistrates and the common people fall short, where will they take from?
translations.idiomatic: When county magistrates and the common people fall short, where will they take from?

sentences.zh: 今東南洊饑，民至骨肉相食，而搜括之令頻行，臣等竊以為不可。」

translations.literal: Now famine recurs in the southeast, and the people have come to eating one another's flesh—yet orders for exactions are issued repeatedly; we deem this unacceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Now famine recurs in the southeast, and the people have come to eating one another's flesh—yet orders for exactions are issued repeatedly; we deem this unacceptable."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: Acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Acknowledgment was returned.

sentences.zh: 已，又劾席書振濟乖方，乞遣官往勘，正其欺罔罪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also impeached Xi Shu for mishandling famine relief, asking that officials be sent to investigate and punish his deception.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he also impeached Xi Shu for mishandling famine relief, asking that officials be sent to investigate and punish his deception.

sentences.zh: 帝方眷書甚，驛召為禮部尚書，不罪也。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then very favorably disposed toward Shu and summoned him by courier to be Minister of Rites; no punishment followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then very favorably disposed toward Shu and summoned him by courier to be Minister of Rites; no punishment followed.

sentences.zh: 初，興獻帝議加皇號，漢卿力爭，至是，又倡眾伏闕。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Prince of Xingxian's imperial title was debated, Hanqing had remonstrated forcefully; now he again led the crowd in prostrating at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Prince of Xingxian's imperial title was debated, Hanqing had remonstrated forcefully; now he again led the crowd in prostrating at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 兩受杖，斥為民。

translations.literal: He was beaten twice and dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten twice and dismissed as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 二十年，言官邢如默、賈準等會薦天下遺賢，及漢卿，終不召。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year remonstrance officials Xing Rumo, Jia Zhun, and others jointly recommended overlooked worthies throughout the empire, including Hanqing—but he was never summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year remonstrance officials Xing Rumo, Jia Zhun, and others jointly recommended overlooked worthies throughout the empire, including Hanqing—but he was never summoned.

sentences.zh: 張原，字士元，三原人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuan, styled Shiyuan, was a native of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan, styled Shiyuan, was a native of Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 9 (1514).

sentences.zh: 授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Scrutiny of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 疏陳汰冗食、慎工作、禁貢獻、明賞罰、廣言路、進德學六事。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth six matters: cutting redundant posts, exercising care in public works, forbidding tribute offerings, clarifying rewards and punishments, broadening the avenue of remonstrance, and advancing moral learning.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he set forth six matters: cutting redundant posts, exercising care in public works, forbidding tribute offerings, clarifying rewards and punishments, broadening the avenue of remonstrance, and advancing moral learning.

sentences.zh: 中言：「天下幅員萬里，一舉事而計臣輒告匱，民貧故也。

translations.literal: Among these he said: "The empire spans ten thousand li; whenever anything is undertaken the finance ministers report shortage—it is because the people are poor.
translations.idiomatic: Among these he said: "The empire spans ten thousand li; whenever anything is undertaken the finance ministers report shortage—it is because the people are poor.

sentences.zh: 民何以貧？

translations.literal: Why are the people poor?
translations.idiomatic: Why are the people poor?

sentences.zh: 守令之裒斂，中臣之貢獻，為之也。

translations.literal: The exactions of prefects and magistrates and the tribute offerings of inner-court eunuchs are what cause it.
translations.idiomatic: It is caused by the exactions of prefects and magistrates and the tribute offerings of inner-court eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 比年軍需雜輸十倍前制，皆取辦守令。

translations.literal: In recent years military levies and miscellaneous contributions have been ten times the former quota, all to be furnished by prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years military levies and miscellaneous contributions have reached ten times the former quota, all of which prefects and magistrates must furnish.

sentences.zh: 守令假以自殖，又十倍於上供。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates use these as pretexts to enrich themselves, taking ten times more again beyond what goes upward.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates use these levies as pretexts to enrich themselves, extracting ten times again what they send upward.

sentences.zh: 民既困矣，而貢獻者復巧立名目，爭新競異，號曰『孝順』。

translations.literal: When the people are already distressed, those making tribute offerings again craft new categories, competing in novelty, calling it "Filial Submission."
translations.idiomatic: When the people are already in distress, tribute-bearers again invent new categories, vying in novelty and calling it "Filial Submission."

sentences.zh: 取於民者十百，進於上者一二，朝廷何樂於此而受之。

translations.literal: What is taken from the people is ten or a hundred parts; what is presented upward is one or two—what pleasure does the court take in receiving this?
translations.idiomatic: They take ten or a hundred parts from the people and present one or two to the throne—what pleasure does the court find in accepting this?

sentences.zh: 人君馭下惟賞與罰。

translations.literal: A ruler governs subordinates solely through reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler governs his subordinates solely through reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 邇者庸才廝養莫不封侯腰玉。

translations.literal: Recently even mediocrities and menials have all been enfeoffed as marquises and girded with jade.
translations.idiomatic: Recently even mediocrities and menials have all been enfeoffed as marquises and girded with jade.

sentences.zh: 或足不出門而受賞，身不履陣而奏功。

translations.literal: Some receive rewards without ever leaving their doors; some report merit without ever treading the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Some receive rewards without ever leaving their doors; others report merit without ever setting foot on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 禦敵者竟未沾恩，覆軍者多至逃罪。

translations.literal: Those who defend against the enemy in the end receive no grace; those who destroy armies often even escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold the enemy at bay receive no reward in the end, while those who lose armies often escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 此士卒所由解體也。」

translations.literal: This is why the troops fall apart."
translations.idiomatic: This is why the troops lose heart and fall apart."

sentences.zh: 疏入，權幸惡之，傳旨謫新添驛丞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the powerful and favored hated it; an edict was transmitted demoting him to deputy post-station master at Xintian.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the powerful and favored hated it, and an edict was transmitted demoting him to deputy post-station master at Xintian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，召復兵科，仍加俸一級。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, he was recalled and restored to the military scrutiny, with one grade added to his salary.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign, he was recalled and restored to the military scrutiny, with one grade added to his salary.

sentences.zh: 南寧伯毛良殺其子，錦衣掌印指揮朱震等多違縱，原先後論之，皆奪職閑住。

translations.literal: Nanning Marquis Mao Liang killed his son; Zhu Zhen, chief seal-bearer and commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and others repeatedly violated discipline and indulged wrongdoing. Zhang Yuan and Mao Yu memorialized about these cases in succession, and all were stripped of office and left idle.
translations.idiomatic: Nanning Marquis Mao Liang killed his son, and Zhu Zhen, chief seal-bearer and commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, among others, repeatedly violated discipline. Zhang Yuan and Mao Yu memorialized about these cases in succession, and all were stripped of office and left idle.

sentences.zh: 帝進張鶴齡昌國公；

translations.literal: The Emperor promoted Zhang Heling to Duke of Changguo;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor promoted Zhang Heling to Duke of Changguo;

sentences.zh: 封陳萬言泰和伯，世襲，授萬言子紹祖尚寶丞；

translations.literal: enfeoffed Chen Wanyan as Marquis of Taihe with hereditary rank, and appointed Wanyan's son Shaozu Assistant Director of the Imperial Observatory;
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffed Chen Wanyan as Marquis of Taihe with hereditary rank, and appointed Wanyan's son Shaozu Assistant Director of the Imperial Observatory;

sentences.zh: 又以外戚蔣泰等五人為錦衣千、百戶。

translations.literal: and further made five maternal relatives including Jiang Tai Embroidered Uniform Guard officers at the thousand- and hundred-household ranks.
translations.idiomatic: and further appointed five maternal relatives, including Jiang Tai, as Embroidered Uniform Guard officers at the thousand- and hundred-household ranks.

sentences.zh: 原抗疏極言，請行裁節。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuan submitted a forceful memorial asking that cuts and economizing be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan submitted a forceful memorial asking that retrenchment and economizing be carried out.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劾建昌侯張延齡強占民地，定國公徐光祚子、外戚玉田伯蔣輪、昌化伯邵蕙家人擅作威福。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached Marquis of Jianchang Zhang Yanling for forcibly seizing private land, and the son of Duke of Dingguo Xu Guangzuo, maternal relative Marquis of Yutian Jiang Lun, and the household of Marquis of Changhua Shao Hui for arrogating authority.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached Marquis of Jianchang Zhang Yanling for forcibly seizing private land, and also the son of Duke of Dingguo Xu Guangzuo, maternal relative Marquis of Yutian Jiang Lun, and the household of Marquis of Changhua Shao Hui for arrogating power and privilege.

sentences.zh: 事雖不盡行，權貴皆震懾。

translations.literal: Though the matters were not fully acted upon, the powerful and noble were all shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Though the matters were not fully carried out, the powerful and noble were all shaken.

sentences.zh: 御史曹嘉素輕險，仿宋範仲淹《百官圖》，分廷臣四等，加以品題。

translations.literal: Censor Cao Jia was by nature frivolous and rash; imitating Song Fan Zhongyan's "Chart of the Hundred Officials," he divided court ministers into four grades and added appraisals.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cao Jia was by nature frivolous and rash; imitating Song Fan Zhongyan's "Chart of the Hundred Officials," he divided court ministers into four grades and added appraisals.

sentences.zh: 給事中安磐疏駁之，言唐王珪之論房玄齡等，本朝解縉之論黃福等，皆承君命而品藻之，未有漫然恣其口吻，如嘉者也。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary An Pan rebutted him in a memorial, saying that Tang Wang Gui's appraisals of Fang Xuanling and others and this dynasty's Xie Jin's appraisals of Huang Fu and others were all by imperial command—never has anyone freely wielded his mouth as Jia has.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary An Pan rebutted him in a memorial, saying that Tang Wang Gui's appraisals of Fang Xuanling and others and this dynasty's Xie Jin's appraisals of Huang Fu and others were all by imperial command—never has anyone freely wielded his tongue as Jia has.

sentences.zh: 玉復言嘉背違成法，變亂國是，乞斥。

translations.literal: Mao Yu again said Jia had violated established law and upset the national consensus, and asked that he be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yu again said Jia had violated established law and upset the national consensus, and asked that he be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝從其言，貶嘉於外。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice and demoted Jia to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed his advice and demoted Jia to an outside post.

sentences.zh: 御史許宗魯為嘉訟，請斥玉，其同官倫以謀亦助為言。

translations.literal: Censor Xu Zonglu pleaded Jia's case and asked that Mao Yu be dismissed; his colleague Censor Lun Yimou also helped speak on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Zonglu pleaded Jia's case and asked that Mao Yu be dismissed; his colleague Censor Lun Yimou also helped speak on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 給事中張原以庶僚聚訟，朝廷為之多事，重損國體，乞身先斥罷。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Yuan, holding that lower officials were gathering in dispute and making the court contentious, thereby gravely harming the dignity of the state, asked that he himself be dismissed first.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Yuan, holding that lower officials were gathering in dispute and making the court contentious, thereby gravely harming the dignity of the state, asked that he himself be dismissed first.

sentences.zh: 玉亦上疏求去，言：「宗魯等知朋友私恩，不顧朝廷大體。

translations.literal: Mao Yu also submitted a memorial requesting leave, saying: "Zonglu and the others value private friendship and know nothing of the greater interest of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yu also submitted a memorial requesting leave, saying: "Zonglu and the others value private friendship and pay no heed to the greater interest of the court.

sentences.zh: 臣一身所系絕微，公論所關甚大，乞罷臣以謝御史。」

translations.literal: What attaches to my person is utterly slight, but what public opinion concerns is very great—I beg that I be dismissed to apologize to the censors."
translations.idiomatic: What attaches to my person is utterly slight, but what public opinion concerns is very great—I beg that I be dismissed to apologize to the censors."

sentences.zh: 帝皆慰留之。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted and retained them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor comforted and retained them all.

sentences.zh: 時宸濠戚屬連逮者數百人，玉奉命往訊，多所全活。

translations.literal: At the time several hundred kinsmen implicated in the Prince of Ning affair were seized in succession; Mao Yu was ordered to interrogate them and saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: At the time several hundred kinsmen implicated in the Prince of Ning affair were seized in succession; Mao Yu was ordered to interrogate them and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 且言宸濠稱亂，由左右貪賂釀成之。

translations.literal: He also said the Prince of Ning's rebellion was brought about by bribe-taking among those close to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He also said the Prince of Ning's rebellion was brought about by bribe-taking among those close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 因劾守臣不死事者，而禁天下有司與藩府交通。

translations.literal: He therefore impeached defending officials who did not die in duty, and forbade officials throughout the empire from communicating with princely establishments.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore impeached defending officials who did not die in the line of duty, and forbade officials throughout the empire from communicating with princely establishments.

sentences.zh: 帝俱從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented to all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assented to all of these.

sentences.zh: 再遷左給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Left Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Left Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋伏闕爭「大禮」，下獲受杖，竟卒。

translations.literal: Soon he prostrated at the palace gate to dispute the "Grand Rites," was brought down and beaten, and in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he prostrated at the palace gate to dispute the "Grand Rites," was brought down and beaten, and in the end died.

sentences.zh: 後贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 裴紹宗，字伯修，渭南人。

translations.literal: Pei Shaozong, styled Bozhu, was a native of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shaozong, styled Bozhu, was a native of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 12 (1517).

sentences.zh: 除海門知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Haimen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Haimen.

sentences.zh: 武宗南巡，受檄署江都事，權幸憚之，供億大省。

translations.literal: During the Wuzong southern tour, he received orders to handle affairs at Jiangdu; the favored ones feared him and supply expenses were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wuzong's southern tour, he received orders to handle affairs at Jiangdu; the favored ones feared him and supply expenses were greatly reduced.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，召入為兵科給事中。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was summoned and made Supervising Secretary in the military scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he was summoned and made Supervising Secretary in the military scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 即疏請法祖定制，言：「太祖貽謀盡善。

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized asking that ancestral institutions be followed, saying: "The founding Emperor's legacy is utterly perfect.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately memorialized asking that ancestral institutions be followed, saying: "The founding Emperor's legacy is utterly perfect.

sentences.zh: 如重大臣，勤視朝，親歷田野，服浣濯衣，種蔬宮中，毀鏤金床，碎水晶漏，造觀心亭，揭《大學衍義》之類，陛下所當繹思祖述。

translations.literal: Such as valuing great ministers, diligently holding court, personally traversing the fields, wearing washed clothes, planting vegetables in the palace, destroying inlaid gold beds, smashing crystal clepsydrae, building the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind, and posting passages from the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning—Your Majesty should deeply ponder and follow the ancestors in these.
translations.idiomatic: Such as valuing great ministers, diligently holding court, personally traversing the fields, wearing washed clothes, planting vegetables in the palace, destroying inlaid gold beds, smashing crystal clepsydrae, building the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind, and posting passages from the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning—Your Majesty should deeply ponder these and follow the ancestors' example.

sentences.zh: 而二三大臣尤宜朝夕納誨，以輔養聖德。

translations.literal: And the two or three great ministers especially ought morning and evening to offer remonstrance, to nurture and foster sacred virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The two or three great ministers especially ought morning and evening to offer remonstrance, to nurture and foster sacred virtue.

sentences.zh: 陛下日御便殿，親儒臣，使耳目不蔽於淫邪，左右不惑於險佞，則君誌素定，治功可成。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty daily presides in the side hall and receives Confucian ministers, so that your ears and eyes are not blocked by licentious evil and those at your side are not misled by dangerous flatterers, then the ruler's purpose will be settled and ordered governance can be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty daily presides in the side hall and receives Confucian ministers, so that your ears and eyes are not blocked by licentious evil and those at your side are not misled by dangerous flatterers, then the ruler's purpose will be settled and ordered governance can be achieved."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 帝欲加興獻帝皇號，紹宗力諫。

translations.literal: When the Emperor wished to add an imperial title to the Prince of Xing, Shaozong remonstrated forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor wished to add an imperial title to the Prince of Xing, Shaozong remonstrated forcefully.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年冬，帝以災異頻仍，欲罷明年郊祀慶成宴。

translations.literal: In the winter of Jiajing 2, because calamities and anomalies recurred frequently, the Emperor wished to cancel next year's suburban sacrifice and the celebration banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jiajing 2 (1523), because calamities and anomalies recurred frequently, the Emperor wished to cancel the next year's suburban sacrifice and the celebration banquet.

sentences.zh: 紹宗言：「祭祀之禮莫重於郊丘，君臣之情必通於宴享。

translations.literal: Shaozong said: "Of sacrificial rites none is weightier than the suburban rites at the mound and altar; of the sentiment between ruler and ministers none fails to pass through banquets and feasts.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong said: "Of sacrificial rites none is weightier than the suburban rites at the mound and altar; of the bond between ruler and ministers none fails to pass through banquets and feasts.

sentences.zh: 往以國戚廢大禮，今且從吉，宜即舉行，豈可以災傷復免。」

translations.literal: Formerly the great rites were suspended on account of imperial mourning; now the mourning period is nearly ended and they should immediately be performed—how can they again be waived because of disaster and harm?"
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the great rites were suspended on account of imperial mourning; now the mourning period is nearly ended and they should immediately be performed—how can they again be waived because of disaster and harm?"

sentences.zh: 修撰唐臯亦言之。

translations.literal: Compiler Tang Gao also spoke to this.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Tang Gao also spoke to this.

sentences.zh: 竟得如禮。

translations.literal: In the end all was conducted according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the end all was conducted according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 明年，以伏闕受杖卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died from beatings received when prostrating at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died from beatings received when prostrating at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 贈官如毛玉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted office like Mao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted office like Mao Yu.

sentences.zh: 王時柯，字敷英，萬安人。

translations.literal: Wang Shike, styled Fuying, was a native of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shike, styled Fuying, was a native of Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 12 (1517).

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed usher.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed usher.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年擢御史，疏言：「桂萼輩以議禮迎合，傳升美官。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 3 he was promoted to censor and memorialized: "Gui E and his ilk, by currying favor through ritual debates, were suddenly promoted to fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 (1524) he was promoted to censor and memorialized: "Gui E and his ilk, by currying favor through ritual debates, were suddenly promoted to fine offices.

sentences.zh: 薛蕙、陳相、段續、胡侍等，連章論劾，實出至公。

translations.literal: Xue Hui, Chen Xiang, Duan Xu, Hu Shi, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching them, truly from utmost public spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Hui, Chen Xiang, Duan Xu, Hu Shi, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching them, truly from utmost public spirit.

sentences.zh: 今佞人超遷而群賢獲罪，恐海內聞之，謂陛下好諛惡直。

translations.literal: Now flatterers are raised while the worthy are punished—I fear when this is heard throughout the realm they will say Your Majesty loves flattery and hates integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Now flatterers are raised while the worthy are punished—I fear that when this is heard throughout the realm, people will say Your Majesty loves flattery and hates integrity.

sentences.zh: 願采忠讜之言，消朋比之禍，特寬蕙等而聽席書、方獻夫辭職，除張璁、桂萼別任，則是非不謬，人情悅服。」

translations.literal: I pray that you heed upright remonstrance, dispel the harm of faction, especially extend clemency to Hui and the others and accept the resignations of Xi Shu and Fang Xianfu, and assign Zhang Cong and Gui E to other posts—then right and wrong will not err and popular sentiment will be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that you heed upright remonstrance, dispel the harm of faction, especially extend clemency to Hui and the others and accept the resignations of Xi Shu and Fang Xianfu, and assign Zhang Cong and Gui E to other posts—then right and wrong will not err and popular sentiment will be satisfied."

sentences.zh: 忤旨切責。

translations.literal: This ran counter to the imperial will and he was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: This ran counter to the imperial will and he was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有伏闕之事，再予杖，除名。

translations.literal: Before long came the prostration at the palace gate; he was beaten again and his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came the prostration at the palace gate; he was beaten again and his name was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 時御史疏爭「大禮」居首者余翺，字大振，定遠人，正德中進士。

translations.literal: At the time the censor who led the memorials disputing the "Grand Rites" was Yu Ao, styled Dazhen, a native of Dingyuan, jinshi under Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the censor who led the memorials disputing the "Grand Rites" was Yu Ao, styled Dazhen, a native of Dingyuan, a jinshi of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年為御史，嘗劾司禮太監張佐蒙蔽罪。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 2 he was censor and once impeached Director of Ceremonial Eunuch Zhang Zuo for concealment and wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2 he was censor and once impeached Director of Ceremonial Eunuch Zhang Zuo for concealment and wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 明年七月，與時柯等被杖戍邊。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the next year he and Shike and others were beaten and exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the next year he and Shike and others were beaten and exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 居戍所十四年。

translations.literal: He remained at his place of exile fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at his place of exile for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 皇子生，赦還。

translations.literal: When a prince was born, an amnesty restored him.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince was born, an amnesty restored him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，時柯、翺皆復官，贈時柯光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Shike and Ao were both restored to office; Shike was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Shike and Ao were both restored to office; Shike was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 鄭本公，朔州衛人。

translations.literal: Zheng Bengong was a native of Shuozhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bengong was a native of Shuozhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 9 (1514).

sentences.zh: 歷御史。

translations.literal: He served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor.

sentences.zh: 武宗不豫，國本未建，本公請慎選宗室親賢者正位東宮，系天下望。

translations.literal: When Wuzong was ill and the heir-apparent had not been established, Bengong asked that a princely kinsman who was close and worthy be carefully chosen for the Eastern Palace, to hold the hopes of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong was ill and the heir-apparent had not been established, Bengong asked that a princely kinsman who was close and worthy be carefully chosen for the Eastern Palace, to hold the hopes of the empire.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，及冬而乾清宮成，帝由文華殿入居之。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, by winter the Qianqing Palace was completed and the Emperor moved from the Wenhua Hall to take up residence there.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, by winter the Qianqing Palace was completed and the Emperor moved from the Wenhua Hall to take up residence there.

sentences.zh: 本公上言：「事之可思者有六。

translations.literal: Bengong submitted a memorial: "There are six matters worthy of reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Bengong submitted a memorial: "There are six matters worthy of reflection.

sentences.zh: 是宮八年營構，一旦告成。

translations.literal: This palace was under construction eight years and was completed in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: This palace was under construction for eight years and was completed in a single day.

sentences.zh: 陛下居安思危，當遠群小，節燕遊，以防一朝之患；

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwelling in security should think of danger—keep petty men at a distance, restrain pleasure outings, to guard against sudden calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, dwelling in security, should think of danger—keep petty men at a distance, restrain pleasure outings, and guard against sudden calamity;

sentences.zh: 重妃配，廣繼嗣，以為萬世之計。

translations.literal: value the consort, broaden succession, as a plan for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: value the consort, broaden succession, as a plan for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 慎終如始，兢兢業業，常若天祖之臨；

translations.literal: Be careful at the end as at the beginning, fearful and reverent, ever as if Heaven and the ancestors were watching;
translations.idiomatic: Be careful at the end as at the beginning, fearful and reverent, ever as if Heaven and the ancestors were watching;

sentences.zh: 求言益切，訪政益勤，用防壅蔽之患。

translations.literal: seek remonstrance the more urgently, inquire into government the more diligently, to guard against the harm of obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: seek remonstrance the more urgently, inquire into government the more diligently, to guard against the harm of obstruction.

sentences.zh: 持聖心，遠貨色，毋溺於鴆毒；

translations.literal: Hold the sacred heart, keep far from wealth and women, and do not drown in poison;
translations.idiomatic: Hold the sacred heart, keep far from wealth and women, and do not drown in poison;

sentences.zh: 重興作，惜財力，永鑒於先朝。」

translations.literal: value construction projects lightly, cherish financial strength, and forever take warning from the previous reign."
translations.idiomatic: value construction projects lightly, cherish financial strength, and forever take warning from the previous reign."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 逾月，帝欲加興獻帝皇號，本公力言不可。

translations.literal: After more than a month the Emperor wished to add an imperial title to the Prince of Xing; Bengong spoke forcefully that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the Emperor wished to add an imperial title to the Prince of Xing; Bengong spoke forcefully that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，出按遼東。

translations.literal: When the Jiajing reign was proclaimed, he went out on provincial inspection in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing reign was proclaimed, he went out on provincial inspection in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 劾罷副總兵張銘、都指揮周輔。

translations.literal: He impeached and dismissed Vice Commander Zhang Ming and Regional Commander Zhou Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and dismissed Vice Commander Zhang Ming and Regional Commander Zhou Fu.

sentences.zh: 還朝，論救給事中劉最，忤旨切責。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he pleaded on behalf of Supervising Secretary Liu Zui, ran counter to the imperial will, and was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he pleaded on behalf of Supervising Secretary Liu Zui, ran counter to the imperial will, and was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，時享太廟，帝不親行。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year, at the seasonal sacrifice to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Emperor did not go in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year, at the seasonal sacrifice to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Emperor did not go in person.

sentences.zh: 本公與同官彭占祺極言遣代非宜，報聞。

translations.literal: Bengong and his colleague Peng Zhanqi spoke forcefully that sending a substitute was improper; acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Bengong and his colleague Peng Zhanqi spoke forcefully that sending a substitute was improper; acknowledgment was returned.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，帝欲考興獻帝，立廟禁中。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year the Emperor wished to enshrine the Prince of Xing and establish a temple within the palace confines.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the next year the Emperor wished to enshrine the Prince of Xing and establish a temple within the palace confines.

sentences.zh: 本公偕同官力爭，謂：「陛下潛邸之日，則為孝宗之侄，興獻王之子。

translations.literal: Bengong joined his colleagues in forceful dispute, saying: "On the days when Your Majesty was in the hidden residence, you were nephew to Xiaozong and son to the Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Bengong joined his colleagues in forceful dispute, saying: "On the days when Your Majesty was in the hidden residence, you were nephew to Xiaozong and son to the Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 臨御之日，則為孝宗之子，興獻帝之侄。

translations.literal: On the day you assumed the throne, you became son to Xiaozong and nephew to the Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day you assumed the throne, you became son to Xiaozong and nephew to the Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 可兩言決也。

translations.literal: This can be decided in two sentences.
translations.idiomatic: This can be decided in two sentences.

sentences.zh: 至立廟大內，實為不經。

translations.literal: As for establishing a temple within the inner palace, it is truly irregular.
translations.idiomatic: As for establishing a temple within the inner palace, it is truly irregular.

sentences.zh: 獻帝之靈既不得入太廟，又空去一國之祀而托享於大內焉。

translations.literal: Since the spirit of the Prince of Xing cannot enter the Imperial Ancestral Temple, you would also void the sacrificial rites of a whole state and entrust his enjoyment of offerings to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Since the spirit of the Prince of Xing cannot enter the Imperial Ancestral Temple, you would also void the sacrificial rites of a whole state and entrust his enjoyment of offerings to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 陛下享太廟，其文曰『嗣皇帝』，於獻帝之廟，又當何稱？

translations.literal: When Your Majesty sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the text reads 'Heir Emperor'—what title then should be used at the temple of the Prince of Xing?"
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the text reads 'Heir Emperor'—what title then should be used at the temple of the Prince of Xing?"

sentences.zh: 愛敬精誠，兩無所屬，獻帝將蹙然不安。」

translations.literal: In love, reverence, and sincerity you would belong fully to neither, and the Prince of Xing would be left ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In love, reverence, and sincerity you would belong fully to neither, and the Prince of Xing would be left deeply ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責其朋言亂政，奪俸三月。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, rebuked them for factional talk that disturbed government, and suspended their salaries for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, rebuked them for factional talk that disturbed government, and suspended their salaries for three months.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，以席書為禮部尚書，召張璁、桂萼入京。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year Xi Shu was made Minister of Rites, and Zhang Cong and Gui E were summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year Xi Shu was appointed Minister of Rites, and Zhang Cong and Gui E were summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 本公偕同官四十四人連章言：「萼首為亂階，璁再肆欺罔，黃綰、黃宗明、方獻夫、席書連匯接踵。

translations.literal: Bengong and forty-four colleagues submitted successive joint memorials saying: "Gui E was first to make the riotous opening; Zhang Cong again wantonly deceived; Huang Guan, Huang Zongming, Fang Xianfu, and Xi Shu followed one after another in a stream.
translations.idiomatic: Bengong and forty-four colleagues submitted successive joint memorials saying: "Gui E was first to make the riotous opening; Zhang Cong again wantonly deceived; Huang Guan, Huang Zongming, Fang Xianfu, and Xi Shu followed one after another in a stream.

sentences.zh: 尚書之命，由中而下。

translations.literal: Appointments as minister come from the interior downward.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments as minister come from the interior downward.

sentences.zh: 行取之旨，已罷再頒。

translations.literal: Edicts for direct selection had been cancelled and were issued again.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts for direct selection had been cancelled and were issued again.

sentences.zh: 大臣因此被逐，言官由之得罪。

translations.literal: Great ministers were thereby expelled; remonstrance officials were punished in consequence.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers were thereby expelled; remonstrance officials were punished in consequence.

sentences.zh: 雖往日瑾、彬之奸，流禍不若是酷也。」

translations.literal: Even the villainy of Jin and Bin in bygone days did not spread calamity so cruel as this."
translations.idiomatic: Even the villainy of Liu Jin and Jiang Bin in bygone days had not spread calamity so cruel as this."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: His advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 已，偕廷臣伏闕哭諫。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, together with court ministers he prostrated at the palace gate and wept in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined court ministers in prostrating at the palace gate and weeping in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 繫獄，廷杖還職。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned, beaten at court, and returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned, beaten at court, and then restored to office.

sentences.zh: 當是時，爭「大禮」者，諸御史中，本公言最切中。

translations.literal: At that time, among the censors disputing the "Grand Rites," Bengong's words were the most incisive.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, among the censors who disputed the "Grand Rites," Bengong's words hit the mark most precisely.

sentences.zh: 尋遷通政參議。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to be Junior Administrator in the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to serve as Junior Administrator in the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 九年不調，以疾請改南京。

translations.literal: For nine years he received no transfer; on grounds of illness he requested reassignment to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: For nine years he received no transfer; citing illness, he requested reassignment to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 乃授大理寺丞，稍遷南京太仆少卿。

translations.literal: He was then made Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and was gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 二十年，言官邢如默、賈準等會薦，詔用不赴，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, remonstrance officials Xing Rumo, Jia Zhun, and others jointly recommended him; an edict summoned him to service but he did not go, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, remonstrance officials Xing Rumo, Jia Zhun, and others jointly recommended him; the Emperor ordered him summoned to office, but he did not come, and he died.

sentences.zh: 張曰韜，字席珍，莆田人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuetao, styled Xizhen, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuetao, styled Xizhen, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 12 (1517).

sentences.zh: 授常州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Prefectural Judge of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Prefectural Judge of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 武宗南巡，江彬縱其黨橫行州縣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong toured south, Jiang Bin allowed his faction to rampage through prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong toured the south, Jiang Bin let his followers rampage through prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 將抵常州，民爭欲亡匿。

translations.literal: As they were about to reach Changzhou, the people all wanted to flee and hide.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to reach Changzhou, the people all wanted to flee and hide.

sentences.zh: 時知府暨武進知縣鹹入覲，曰韜兼綰府縣印，召父老約曰：「彬黨至，若等力與格。」

translations.literal: At the time the prefect and the district magistrate of Wujin had all gone to audience; Yuetao held both the prefectural and county seals, summoned the elders, and pledged: "When Bin's faction arrives, you must resist them with all your strength."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the prefect and the district magistrate of Wujin had all gone to audience at court; Yuetao held both the prefectural and county seals, summoned the elders, and made this pact: "When Bin's followers arrive, resist them with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 又釋囚徒，令與丐者各具瓦石待。

translations.literal: He also released prisoners and had them and beggars each prepare tiles and stones and wait.
translations.idiomatic: He also released prisoners and had them and beggars each prepare tiles and stones and stand ready.

sentences.zh: 已，彬黨果累騎來。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, Bin's faction did come in a long train of mounted men.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Bin's followers did arrive in a long train of mounted men.

sentences.zh: 父老直遮之境上，曰：「常州比歲災，物力大屈，無可啖若曹。

translations.literal: The elders blocked them directly at the border of the jurisdiction, saying: "Changzhou has suffered disasters these recent years; resources are greatly exhausted, and there is nothing to feed you lot.
translations.idiomatic: The elders blocked them directly at the boundary of the jurisdiction, saying: "Changzhou has suffered disasters in recent years; its resources are greatly depleted, and there is nothing with which to feed you.

sentences.zh: 府中惟一張推官，一錢不入，即欲具芻秣，亦無以辦。」

translations.literal: In the prefecture there is only one Investigating Judge Zhang; not a single coin has entered his hands—even if we wished to provide fodder and grain, we have no means to do so."
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture there is only Investigating Judge Zhang; not a single coin has entered his hands—even if we wished to provide fodder and grain, we could not manage it."

sentences.zh: 言已，彬黨疑有他變，乃稍退，馳使告彬。

translations.literal: When they had finished speaking, Bin's faction suspected some other plot and withdrew somewhat, sending a messenger at full speed to tell Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When they had finished, Bin's men suspected some other plot and fell back somewhat, dispatching a messenger at full speed to tell Bin.

sentences.zh: 曰韜即上書巡按御史言狀。

translations.literal: Yuetao immediately submitted a memorial to the touring censor reporting the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuetao immediately submitted a memorial to the touring censor reporting what had happened.

sentences.zh: 御史東郊行部過常州，謂曰：「事迫矣，彬將以他事縛君。」

translations.literal: Censor Dong Jiao, on tour through the jurisdiction, passed Changzhou and said to him: "The matter is urgent; Bin will bind you on some other charge."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dong Jiao, inspecting the circuit, passed through Changzhou and said to him: "The matter is urgent; Bin will have you seized on some other charge."

sentences.zh: 命曰韜登己舟先發，自以小舟尾之。

translations.literal: He ordered Yuetao to board his own boat and depart first, while he himself followed in a small boat.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yuetao to board his own boat and set out first, while he himself followed in a small craft.

sentences.zh: 彬黨果大至，索曰韜，誤截御史舟。

translations.literal: Bin's faction did arrive in force, seeking Yuetao, and by mistake intercepted the censor's boat.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's men did arrive in force, seeking Yuetao, and by mistake intercepted the censor's boat.

sentences.zh: 郊使嚴捕截舟者，而陰令緩之。

translations.literal: Jiao sent men to arrest the boat-interceptors sternly, but secretly ordered them to proceed slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao sent men to arrest the boat-interceptors with a show of severity, but secretly ordered them to proceed slowly.

sentences.zh: 其黨恐御史上聞，鹹散去，曰韜遂免。

translations.literal: His faction, fearing the censor would report upward, all dispersed, and Yuetao was thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: His men, fearing the censor would report upward, all dispersed, and Yuetao was thus spared.

sentences.zh: 彬亦戒其黨毋擾，由是常以南諸府得安。

translations.literal: Bin also warned his faction not to disturb the region, and from this the various prefectures south of Changzhou enjoyed peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bin also warned his followers not to harass the region, and from then on the prefectures south of Changzhou enjoyed peace.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，召為御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was summoned to serve as censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was summoned to serve as censor.

sentences.zh: 楊廷和等之爭織造也，曰韜亦上言：「陛下既稱閣臣所奏惟愛主惜民，是明知織造之害矣。

translations.literal: When Yang Tinghe and others disputed silk weaving, Yuetao also submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has already declared that what the Grand Secretariat reported was solely love for the sovereign and pity for the people—this means you clearly know the harm of silk weaving.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Tinghe and others disputed imperial silk weaving, Yuetao also submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has already declared that what the Grand Secretariat reported was solely love for the sovereign and pity for the people—you clearly know the harm of silk weaving.
