sentences.zh: 既知之，而猶不已，實由信任大臣弗專，而群小為政也。

translations.literal: Once you know it and yet do not stop, it is truly because trust in great ministers is not exclusive, and the petty crowd holds power.
translations.idiomatic: Once you know this and yet do not stop, it is truly because you do not place exclusive trust in your great ministers, and petty men hold power instead.

sentences.zh: 自古未有群小蒙蔽於內，而大臣能盡忠於外者。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been a case in which petty men deceived within, while great ministers could exhaust loyalty without.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity there has never been a case in which petty men deceived within the palace while great ministers could serve with full loyalty without.

sentences.zh: 崔文輩二三小人嘗濁亂先朝，今復蒙惑聖衷，竊弄威福。

translations.literal: Two or three petty men such as Cui Wen once muddied and disturbed the former court; now they again beguile the imperial heart and secretly wield authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Two or three petty men such as Cui Wen once muddied and disturbed the former court; now they beguile Your Majesty again and secretly wield authority and favor.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何任其逞私，不早加斥逐哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, how can you let them indulge their private desires and not drive them out early?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, how can you let them indulge their private desires and not drive them out at once?

sentences.zh: 臣聞織造一官，行金數萬方得之。

translations.literal: I have heard that to obtain one post in silk weaving, one must pay tens of thousands in cash.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to obtain one post in silk weaving, one must pay tens of thousands in cash.

sentences.zh: 既營之以重資，而欲其不責償於下，此必無之事也。」

translations.literal: Once one has invested a heavy sum to obtain it, yet expects that he will not seek repayment from those below—this is surely impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Once one has invested a heavy sum to obtain it, yet expects that he will not seek repayment from those below—this is surely impossible."

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not heed it.

sentences.zh: 席書以中旨拜尚書，曰韜與同官胡瓊各抗疏力爭。

translations.literal: When Xi Shu was appointed minister by secret edict, Yuetao and his colleague Hu Qiong each submitted forceful remonstrance memorials in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Shu was appointed minister by secret edict, Yuetao and his colleague Hu Qiong each submitted forceful remonstrance memorials in opposition.

sentences.zh: 既受杖，猶占疏劾奸人陳洸罪。

translations.literal: After receiving the beating, he still submitted a memorial impeaching the villain Chen Guang of his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the beating, he still submitted a memorial impeaching the villain Chen Guang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，竟死。

translations.literal: Before long he died in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，追贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously ennobled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was posthumously ennobled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 胡瓊，字國華，南平人。

translations.literal: Hu Qiong, styled Guohua, was a native of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qiong, styled Guohua, was a native of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Zhengde 6 (1511).

sentences.zh: 由慈溪知縣入為御史。

translations.literal: From district magistrate of Cixi he entered service as censor.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as district magistrate of Cixi he entered service as censor.

sentences.zh: 歷按貴州、浙江有聲。

translations.literal: He successively inspected Guizhou and Zhejiang and gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: He successively inspected Guizhou and Zhejiang and gained renown.

sentences.zh: 哭諫，受杖卒。

translations.literal: He wept in remonstrance, received the beating, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He wept in remonstrance, received the beating, and died.

sentences.zh: 後贈官如曰韜。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously ennobled the same as Yuetao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received the same posthumous ennoblement as Yuetao.

sentences.zh: 楊淮，字東川，無錫人。

translations.literal: Yang Huai, styled Dongchuan, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huai, styled Dongchuan, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 12 (1517).

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and was twice promoted to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and was promoted twice to Director.

sentences.zh: 始監京倉，革胥徒積弊殆盡。

translations.literal: At first he supervised the capital granaries and reformed accumulated abuses of clerks and runners nearly to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: At first he supervised the capital granaries and reformed accumulated abuses of clerks and runners almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 繼監淮、通二倉，罷中官茶果之供，除囤基及額外席草費。

translations.literal: Next he supervised the granaries at Huai'an and Tongzhou, abolished eunuch provisions of tea and fruit, and eliminated storage-base charges and extra fees for reed-mat bedding.
translations.idiomatic: Next he supervised the granaries at Huai'an and Tongzhou, abolished eunuch provisions of tea and fruit, and eliminated storage-base charges and extra fees for reed-mat bedding.

sentences.zh: 最後監內庫，奄人例有供饋，淮悉絕之。

translations.literal: Finally he supervised the inner treasury; eunuchs customarily received supplies and gifts—Huai cut them all off.
translations.idiomatic: Finally he supervised the inner treasury; eunuchs customarily received supplies and gifts—Huai cut them all off.

sentences.zh: 公勤廉慎，為尚書孫交、秦金所重。

translations.literal: Public-spirited, diligent, incorrupt, and careful, he was valued by Ministers Sun Jiao and Qin Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Public-spirited, diligent, incorrupt, and careful, he was valued by Ministers Sun Jiao and Qin Jin.

sentences.zh: 伏闕受杖，月余卒。

translations.literal: He prostrated at the palace gate, received the beating, and died after more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated at the palace gate, received the beating, and died after more than a month.

sentences.zh: 囊無一物，家人賣屋以斂。

translations.literal: His purse held not a single thing; his family sold their house to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: His purse held not a single thing; his family sold their house to bury him.

sentences.zh: 金與淮同里，為經紀歸其喪。

translations.literal: Jin was from the same district as Huai and made arrangements to return his remains home.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jin was from the same district as Huai and made arrangements to return his remains home.

sentences.zh: 後贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously ennobled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously ennobled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 申良，字延賢，高平人。

translations.literal: Shen Liang, styled Yanxian, was a native of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Liang, styled Yanxian, was a native of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 登鄉薦，授招遠知縣。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial recommendation and was appointed district magistrate of Zhaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial recommendation and was appointed district magistrate of Zhaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 山東盜起，良豫為戰守具。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Shandong, Liang prepared in advance the means for defense and battle.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Shandong, Liang prepared in advance the means for defense and battle.

sentences.zh: 盜至，追擊至黃縣，俘斬數百人。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, he pursued them to Huang County and captured and beheaded several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived, he pursued them to Huang County and captured and beheaded several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 已，復至，再破走之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they came again, and he defeated and drove them off once more.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they came again, and he defeated and drove them off once more.

sentences.zh: 歷知諸城、良鄉。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Zhucheng and Liangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as magistrate of Zhucheng and Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 權貴人往來要索，良悉拒之。

translations.literal: Powerful and noble persons coming and going demanded favors, and Liang refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful and noble persons coming and going demanded favors, and Liang refused them all.

sentences.zh: 進安吉知州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Anji.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Anji.

sentences.zh: 錦衣葉瓊倚錢寧勢奪民田，良讞還之民。

translations.literal: Ye Qiong of the Embroidered Uniform Guard relied on Qian Ning's power to seize commoners' land; Liang judged the case and returned it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Qiong of the Embroidered Uniform Guard relied on Qian Ning's power to seize commoners' land; Liang judged the case and returned it to the people.

sentences.zh: 瓊因嗾奸人誣奏良，事竟得白。

translations.literal: Qiong therefore instigated villains to falsely accuse Liang, but in the end the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong therefore instigated villains to falsely accuse Liang, but in the end the matter was cleared.

sentences.zh: 稍遷常州同知，入為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice Prefect of Changzhou and entered service as Section Member in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Vice Prefect of Changzhou and entered service as Section Member in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與淮俱杖死。

translations.literal: Together with Huai he died from the beating.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Huai he died from the beating.

sentences.zh: 贈太僕少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 招遠民懷其政，繪像祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Zhaoyuan cherished his governance and painted his portrait to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Zhaoyuan cherished his governance and painted his portrait to worship him.

sentences.zh: 張澯，字景川，廣東順德人。

translations.literal: Zhang Can, styled Jingchuan, was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Can, styled Jingchuan, was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 祖善昭，四川僉事，謫臨江通判。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shanshao was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Sichuan and was demoted to Vice Prefect of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shanshao was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Sichuan and was demoted to Vice Prefect of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 先是，練子寧親黨戍臨江者八十余人，善昭上書曰：「子寧忠貫日月，太宗謂『若使子寧在，朕固當用之』。

translations.literal: Earlier, more than eighty relatives and associates of Lian Zining who were exiled to Linjiang—Shanshao submitted a memorial saying: "Zining's loyalty pierced sun and moon; Taizong said, 'If Zining were alive, I would certainly employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, more than eighty relatives and associates of Lian Zining who were exiled to Linjiang—Shanshao submitted a memorial saying: "Zining's loyalty pierced sun and moon; Taizong said, 'If Zining were alive, I would certainly employ him.

sentences.zh: 仁宗亦謂『方孝孺等忠臣』。

translations.literal: Renzong also called 'Fang Xiaoru and others loyal ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: Renzong also called 'Fang Xiaoru and others loyal ministers.'

sentences.zh: 夫既忠之矣，何外親末屬，尚以奸惡賜配，百年不宥哉？」

translations.literal: Since they were already loyal, why should distant kin and minor dependents still be punished by exile for wickedness and not be pardoned for a hundred years?"
translations.idiomatic: Since they were already loyal, why should distant kin and minor dependents still be punished by exile for wickedness and not be pardoned for a hundred years?"

sentences.zh: 疏雖不行，中外皆壯之。

translations.literal: Although the memorial was not adopted, within and without all admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Although the memorial was not adopted, people throughout the empire admired him.

sentences.zh: 澯登正德九年進士，授建平知縣。

translations.literal: Can passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Zhengde and was appointed district magistrate of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Can passed the jinshi in the ninth year of the Zhengde reign and was appointed district magistrate of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 忤巡江御史賀洪，改調廣昌。

translations.literal: He offended Yangtze-inspecting Censor He Hong and was transferred to Guangchang.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Yangtze-inspecting Censor He Hong and was transferred to Guangchang.

sentences.zh: 訟洪罪，洪坐削籍。

translations.literal: He sued Hong for crimes, and Hong was punished by having his name struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He sued Hong for crimes, and Hong was punished by having his name struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 澯自廣昌遷禮部主事，監督會同館。

translations.literal: Can moved from Guangchang to Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites, supervising the Hall of Joint Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Can moved from Guangchang to Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites, supervising the Hall of Joint Audience.

sentences.zh: 尚書王瓊與都御史彭澤有隙，以澤遣使土魯番許金幣贖哈密城印為澤罪，嗾番人在館者暴澤過惡，誘澯為署牒，且曰：「澤所為，南宋覆轍也。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Qiong and Censor-in-Chief Peng Ze were at odds; taking as Ze's crime that Ze had sent envoys to Turfan promising gold and coin to redeem the seal of Hami city, he incited the foreign envoys in the hall to expose Ze's faults and wickedness, and tempted Can to sign the document, saying: "What Ze did repeats the overturned track of the Southern Song.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Qiong and Censor-in-Chief Peng Ze were at odds; citing as Ze's crime that Ze had sent envoys to Turfan promising gold and coin to redeem the seal of Hami city, he incited the foreign envoys in the hall to expose Ze's faults and wickedness, and tempted Can to sign the document, saying: "What Ze did repeats the overturned track of the Southern Song.

sentences.zh: 事成當顯擢。」

translations.literal: When the affair succeeds you will be conspicuously promoted."
translations.idiomatic: When the affair succeeds you will be conspicuously promoted."

sentences.zh: 澯力拒曰：「王公誤矣。

translations.literal: Can forcefully refused, saying: "Lord Wang is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Can forcefully refused, saying: "Lord Wang is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 澤與土魯番檄具在，豈宋和戎比。

translations.literal: Ze's dispatches with Turfan are all extant—how can this be compared to the Southern Song making peace?
translations.idiomatic: Ze's dispatches with Turfan are all extant—how can this be compared to the Southern Song making peace?

sentences.zh: 昔範仲淹亦嘗致書元昊，寧獨澤也。」

translations.literal: In the past Fan Zhongyan also once sent letters to Yuan Hao—why should Ze alone be blamed?"
translations.idiomatic: In the past Fan Zhongyan also once sent letters to Yuan Hao—why should Ze alone be blamed?"

sentences.zh: 不肯署。

translations.literal: He refused to sign.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 尋進員外郎，受杖死。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Section Member and died from the beating.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Section Member and died from the beating.

sentences.zh: 仵瑜，字忠父，蒲圻人。

translations.literal: Wu Yu, styled Zhongfu, was a native of Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu, styled Zhongfu, was a native of Puqi.

sentences.zh: 父紳，工部主事。

translations.literal: His father Shen was Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen was Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 瑜少有誌操，正德十二年釋褐，即謝病去。

translations.literal: Yu from youth had aspiration and integrity; in the twelfth year of Zhengde, upon taking office he immediately resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yu from youth had aspiration and integrity; in the twelfth year of the Zhengde reign, upon taking office he immediately resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 起補禮部主事，復引疾歸。

translations.literal: He was recalled to fill a vacancy as Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites and again cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to fill a vacancy as Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites and again cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，起故官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 疏陳勤聖學、篤親親、開言路、敬大臣、選諍臣、去浮屠、拯困窮、重守令、修武備、儲人材十事。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters: diligence in sacred learning, deepening kinship bonds, opening the avenue of speech, reverencing great ministers, selecting remonstrating ministers, removing Buddhist monks, rescuing the distressed and poor, emphasizing magistrates and prefects, repairing military preparedness, and storing up talent.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters: diligence in sacred learning, deepening kinship bonds, opening the avenue of speech, reverencing great ministers, selecting remonstrating ministers, removing Buddhist monks, rescuing the distressed and poor, emphasizing magistrates and prefects, repairing military preparedness, and storing up talent.

sentences.zh: 已，竟死杖下。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died under the beating in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died under the beating.

sentences.zh: 臧應奎，字賢徵，長興人。

translations.literal: Zang Yingkui, styled Xianzheng, was a native of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Yingkui, styled Xianzheng, was a native of Changxing.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 12 (1517).

sentences.zh: 授南京車駕主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk in the Nanjing Directorate of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Clerk in the Nanjing Directorate of Transport.

sentences.zh: 進貢中官索舟逾額，力裁損之。

translations.literal: Tribute eunuchs demanded boats beyond the quota, and he forcefully cut and reduced them.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute eunuchs demanded boats beyond the quota, and he forcefully cut and reduced them.

sentences.zh: 中官遣卒嘩於部，叱左右執之，遁去。

translations.literal: A eunuch sent soldiers to make an uproar at the directorate; he shouted at those beside him to seize them, and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch's men raised a commotion at the directorate, he ordered his attendants to seize them, and they fled.

sentences.zh: 父所生母卒，法不得承重，執私喪三年。

translations.literal: His father's concubine who bore him died; by law he could not assume principal mourning obligations, and he observed private mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When the concubine who bore him for his father died, the law did not permit him to assume principal mourning, so he observed private mourning for three years.

sentences.zh: 入為禮部主事，未幾杖死。

translations.literal: He entered service as Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites and not long afterward died from the beating.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites and soon died from the beating.

sentences.zh: 應奎受業湛若水之門，以聖賢自期。

translations.literal: Yingkui studied under Zhan Ruoshui and set his heart on matching the sages.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui studied under Zhan Ruoshui and aspired to live like the sages.

sentences.zh: 嘗過文廟，慨然謂其友曰「吾輩歿，亦當俎豆其間」，其立誌如此。

translations.literal: Once passing the Temple of Literature, he said feelingly to his friend, "When we die, we too should receive sacrificial offerings here"—such was the resolve he formed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing the Temple of Literature, he said feelingly to a friend, "When we are gone, we too should be honored with offerings in this hall"—such was the ambition he set for himself.

sentences.zh: 郎中胡璉，字重器，新喻人。

translations.literal: Director Hu Lian, styled Chongqi, was a native of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: Director Hu Lian, styled Chongqi, was a native of Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士，官刑部。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde; he served in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Zhengde 6 (1511), he served in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 嘗諫武宗南巡受杖。

translations.literal: Once remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour and received a beating.
translations.idiomatic: He once remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's planned southern tour and was beaten for it.

sentences.zh: 主事余禎，字興邦，奉新人。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yu Zhen, styled Xingbang, was a native of Fengxin.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Yu Zhen, styled Xingbang, was a native of Fengxin.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 9 (1514).

sentences.zh: 司務李可登，字思善，輝縣人。

translations.literal: Registrar Li Kedeng, styled Sishan, was a native of Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Li Kedeng, styled Sishan, was a native of Huixian.

sentences.zh: 弘治末鄉薦。

translations.literal: Recommended in the provincial examinations at the end of the Hongzhi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations at the end of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 俱官兵部。

translations.literal: All served in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: All three served in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 可登素慷慨，以忠義自許，竟如其誌。

translations.literal: Kedeng was by nature generous and pledged himself to loyalty and righteousness, and in the end fulfilled that resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Kedeng was by nature high-minded and pledged himself to loyalty and righteousness—and in the end he fulfilled that pledge.

sentences.zh: 戶部主事安璽，宛平人。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk An Xi of the Ministry of Revenue was a native of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: An Xi, Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, was a native of Wanping.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixteenth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Zhengde 16 (1521).

sentences.zh: 刑部主事殷承敘，江夏人。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yin Chengxu of the Ministry of Punishments was a native of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chengxu, Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, was a native of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 9 (1514).

sentences.zh: 穆宗嗣位，贈璉太常少卿，澯太仆少卿，瑜、應奎、承敘、璽、禎光祿少卿，可登寺丞。

translations.literal: When Muzong succeeded to the throne, Lian was posthumously granted Vice Minister of Rites, Can Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Yu, Yingkui, Chengxu, Xi, and Zhen Vice Ministers of the Imperial Household, and Kedeng Assistant Director of a Temple Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, Lian was posthumously granted Vice Minister of Rites, Can Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Yu, Yingkui, Chengxu, Xi, and Zhen Vice Ministers of the Imperial Household, and Kedeng Assistant Director of a Temple Directorate.

sentences.zh: 諸臣伏闕爭「大禮」，皆得罪。

translations.literal: The various officials prostrated at the palace gate to dispute the "Grand Rites," and all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: The various officials who prostrated at the palace gate to dispute the Great Rites were all punished.

sentences.zh: 楠方巡按雲南，馳疏言：「人臣事君，阿意者未必忠，犯顏者未必悖。

translations.literal: Nan was then on tour inspecting Yunnan and sent an urgent memorial saying: "In serving the ruler, ministers who toady are not necessarily loyal, and those who risk his displeasure are not necessarily disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Nan was then touring Yunnan as investigating censor and sent an urgent memorial: "In serving the sovereign, ministers who toady are not necessarily loyal, and those who speak against his will are not necessarily treacherous.

sentences.zh: 今群臣伏闕呼號，或榜掠殞身，或間關謫戍，不意聖明之朝，而忠良獲罪若此。

translations.literal: Now the officials prostrate at the palace gate crying out; some are flogged to death, some traverse hardships to exile and garrison service—I never expected that in so enlightened a court, loyal and good men would be punished thus.
translations.idiomatic: Now the officials prostrate themselves at the palace gate crying out; some are flogged to death, some are sent on the hard road to banishment and garrison duty—who would have thought that in so enlightened a court, the loyal and upright would be punished like this?

sentences.zh: 乞復生者之職，恤死者之家，庶以收納人心，全君臣之義。」

translations.literal: I beg that the living be restored to office and the dead that their families be comforted, so that hearts may be won back and the bond between ruler and minister be kept whole."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the living be restored to office and the families of the dead be given relief, so that you may win back the people's hearts and preserve the full bond between ruler and minister."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，遣緹騎逮治，言官論救皆不納。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sent mounted guards to arrest and punish him; censorial officials pleaded for his rescue, but none was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, sent mounted guards to arrest and prosecute him, and rejected every attempt by censorial officials to intercede.

sentences.zh: 既至，下鎮撫獄掠治，復廷杖之，削其籍。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison for interrogation under torture, was again beaten at court, and had his name struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he was sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison for interrogation under torture, flogged again at court, and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸人既死，廷臣莫敢上聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the men had died, no court minister dared report it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after these men had died, no court minister dared bring word to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後府經歷俞敬奏言：「學士豐熙等皆以冒觸宸嚴，系獄拷訊。

translations.literal: Later, Yu Jing, an administration clerk in a prefectural office, submitted a memorial saying: "Academician Feng Xi and others have all been imprisoned and interrogated under torture for having offended the imperial majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Yu Jing, an administration clerk in a prefectural office, submitted a memorial: "Academician Feng Xi and others have all been imprisoned and interrogated under torture for having offended the imperial majesty.

sentences.zh: 諸臣跡雖狂悖，心實忠誠。

translations.literal: Although the conduct of these officials was wild and perverse, their hearts were truly loyal and devoted.
translations.idiomatic: Although these officials' conduct seemed wild and perverse, their hearts were truly loyal.

sentences.zh: 今聞給事裴紹宗、編修王相、主事余禎等俱已死，熙等在獄者亦垂亡矣。

translations.literal: Now I hear that Supervising Secretary Pei Shaozong, Compiler Wang Xiang, Chief Clerk Yu Zhen, and others have all died, and those still in prison like Xi are also on the point of death.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear that Supervising Secretary Pei Shaozong, Compiler Wang Xiang, Chief Clerk Yu Zhen, and others have all died, and those still in prison, such as Xi, are also near death.

sentences.zh: 其呻吟衽席，創重不能起者，又不知凡幾。

translations.literal: Of those groaning on their pallets, their wounds so severe they cannot rise, there is no knowing how many more.
translations.idiomatic: Of those groaning on their sickbeds, too gravely wounded to rise, there is no knowing how many more there are.

sentences.zh: 竊惟獻皇帝神主已奉迎入廟，正宜赦過宥罪，章大孝於天下。

translations.literal: I reflect that the spirit tablet of the Prince of Xingxian has already been welcomed into the temple—it is precisely the time to pardon transgressions and grant forgiveness, displaying great filial piety to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the spirit tablet of the Prince of Xingxian has already been welcomed into the ancestral temple—this is precisely the moment to pardon offenses and grant forgiveness, displaying great filial piety to the empire.

sentences.zh: 望霽雷霆之威，施雨露之澤。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will clear away the thunder of wrath and bestow the favor of rain and dew.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will set aside the thunder of wrath and bestow the grace of rain and dew.

sentences.zh: 已死者恤其後，垂亡者宥其身，使人臣無復以言為諱，宗社之幸也。」

translations.literal: Give relief to the families of the dead, grant pardon to those near death, and let ministers no longer take speech as something to be avoided—for that would be the fortune of altars and state."
translations.idiomatic: Comfort the families of the dead, grant pardon to those near death, and let your ministers speak without fear of reproach—this would be a blessing for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 通政司經歷李繼先亦上言：「陛下追崇尊號，乃人子至情，誠不容已。

translations.literal: Li Jixian, an administration clerk in the Office of Transmission, also submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty's elevation of the honored title is the utmost feeling of a son and truly cannot be withheld.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixian, an administration clerk in the Office of Transmission, also submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty's elevation of the honored title is a son's deepest feeling and truly cannot be withheld.

sentences.zh: 群臣一時冒觸天威，重得罪譴，死者遂十余人。

translations.literal: The officials once offended the heavenly majesty and received heavy punishment; more than ten died.
translations.idiomatic: The officials once offended the imperial majesty and suffered heavy punishment; more than ten of them died.

sentences.zh: 大臣紛紛去位，小臣茍默自容。

translations.literal: Great ministers have one after another left office, and lesser ministers are content to keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers have left office one after another, and lesser ministers are content to keep silent.

sentences.zh: 今日大同告變，曾無一人進一疏、畫一策者，則小大之臣，誌不奮而氣不揚，亦可見矣。

translations.literal: Today Datong reports an uprising, yet not a single person submits a memorial or offers a plan—thus among ministers great and small, the will does not stir and the spirit does not lift: this is plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: Today Datong reports an uprising, yet not one person submits a memorial or offers a plan—among ministers great and small alike, the will does not stir and the spirit does not lift. This is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 乞錄恤已死，赦還謫戍，追復去國諸臣，而在位者委任寬假之，使各陳邊計。

translations.literal: I beg that the dead be recorded and given relief, the banished to garrison service be pardoned and returned, the officials who left office be restored, and those still in office be entrusted with leniency so that each may offer plans for the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the dead be honored and their families relieved, those banished to garrison service be pardoned and returned, the officials who left office be restored, and those still in office be given latitude so that each may present plans for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 臣愚不勝惓惓。」

translations.literal: Your humble subject's foolishness cannot overcome earnest devotion."
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject is overcome with earnest devotion."

sentences.zh: 帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The emperor paid attention to none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed to any of it.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，御史王懋言：「廷臣以議禮死杖下者十有七人，其父母妻子顛沛可憫，乞賜優恤，贈官錄蔭。」

translations.literal: The next year, in the third month, Censor Wang Mao submitted a memorial: "Seventeen court officials died under the rod for disputing the rites; their parents, wives, and children have suffered distress that merits pity. I beg that generous relief be granted, with posthumous offices and hereditary privilege."
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the third month, Censor Wang Mao submitted a memorial: "Seventeen court officials died under the rod for disputing the rites; their parents, wives, and children have suffered wretchedly—this merits pity. I beg that generous relief be granted, with posthumous offices and hereditary privilege."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謫懋四川高縣典史。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and demoted Mao to Record Clerk of Gaoxian in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demoted Mao to record clerk of Gaoxian in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 逾數日，而楠疏至。

translations.literal: A few days later Nan's memorial arrived.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Nan's memorial arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，遂逮治削籍。

translations.literal: The emperor grew even angrier, and had him arrested, punished, and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew even angrier and had Nan arrested, prosecuted, and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 六年春，以災變修省，從吏部言量與楠一官，得吉水教諭。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, owing to disaster omens and self-examination, following the Ministry of Personnel's advice Nan was measured out one office and became Instructor at Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year, when disaster omens prompted self-examination, the Ministry of Personnel recommended granting Nan an office; he received the post of instructor at Jishui.

sentences.zh: 終南寧知府。

translations.literal: In the end he served as Prefect of Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Nanning.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「大禮」之爭，群臣至撼門慟哭，亦過激且戇矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: In the dispute over the "Grand Rites," the officials went so far as to beat on the gate and weep in grief—this was excessive and reckless.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: In the dispute over the Great Rites, the officials went so far as to beat on the gate and weep aloud—excessive and rash, to be sure.

sentences.zh: 然再受廷杖，或死或斥，廢錮終身，抑何慘也。

translations.literal: Yet being beaten at court twice, some dying and some banished, locked out for life—how cruel indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were flogged at court a second time; some died, some were banished, and others were shut out for life—how cruel indeed.

sentences.zh: 楊慎博物洽聞，於文學為優。

translations.literal: Yang Shen was broadly learned and well informed, outstanding in literary scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen was broadly learned and widely read, unsurpassed in literary scholarship.

sentences.zh: 王思、張翀諸人，或納諫武宗之朝，或抗論世宗初政，侃侃鑿鑿，死節官下，非徒意氣奮發立效一時已也。

translations.literal: Wang Si, Zhang Chong, and the others—some remonstrating in the reign of Wuzong, some disputing the early policies of Shizong—spoke forthrightly and with conviction, dying in office for their principles; they were not merely men whose spirited zeal flared up to produce an effect for a moment and no more.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si, Zhang Chong, and the others—some remonstrating under Emperor Wuzong, some disputing the early policies of Emperor Shizong—spoke forthrightly and with deep conviction, dying in office for principle; they were not merely men whose ardor flared up for a moment and then faded.
